definition_zh: 讲师；讲课人；（英国）大学讲师
definition_en: a person who gives lectures, especially a teacher at a university or college below professor rank
core_image: 讲台后一个人对着满堂听众大声念读讲稿
scene: 讲座开始前，学生把书本摊开在桌上。The lecturer paused, looked up from her notes and waited for the room to fall silent.
sceneCN: 这里 lecturer 是「讲课人」（第 1 个义项：在课堂上对着听众讲授的人）；句意：讲师抬起头，从讲稿上移开目光，等全场安静下来。

derivatives.zh: lectus（读）派生的名词与动词，指「讲座」或「讲课」，是 lecturer 的基础词
lecturer 加后缀 -ship 构成的职位名词，义为「讲师职位」
lecture 加动名词后缀 -ing，义为「讲课；授课」
同出拉丁语 legere（阅读），指读经者所站的「讲台；读经台」，与 lecturer 读同一词根

senses.title: A person who gives a lecture
senses.definition: someone who stands before an audience and delivers a talk or a taught lesson
senses.definitionCN: 站在听众面前讲授一节课或一场演讲的人
senses.example: The lecturer spoke for an hour about water pollution.
senses.exampleCN: 讲课人就水污染讲了一个小时。
senses.why: The verb lecture means to deliver a spoken talk, and -er names the person who does that action.
senses.whyCN: 动词 lecture 意为「讲授、作演讲」，后缀 -er 标记执行这一动作的人，所以 lecturer 就是「讲课的人」。

senses.title: A university teacher below professor
senses.definition: a teaching post at a British university or college, ranking below a professor
senses.definitionCN: 英国大学或学院里低于教授级别的教学职位
senses.example: She was appointed lecturer in history at the age of twenty-nine.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十九岁时被聘为历史学讲师。
senses.why: Because lecturing is the daily duty of junior academic staff, the -er noun became the name of that paid rank.
senses.whyCN: 因为讲课是年轻教师的本职工作，「讲课的人」这个称呼自然固定为一个职位的名称。

senses.title: A visiting speaker on a special topic
senses.definition: a guest speaker invited to a course, conference, or public event for one particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 被邀请为某门课程、会议或公开活动专门演讲的嘉宾
senses.example: A guest lecturer from the museum explained how the coins were dated.
senses.exampleCN: 一位来自博物馆的客座讲者讲解了钱币是如何断代的。
senses.why: The role sense extends easily to anyone invited to lecture, even without a permanent teaching position.
senses.whyCN: 从固定职位向外一推，临时被请来围绕某主题发言的人也属于「讲课的人」。

senses.title: A person who scolds with long words
senses.definition: a person who talks at others in a long and self-important way
senses.definitionCN: 说话冗长、自以为是地对别人说教的人
senses.example: My uncle turns into a lecturer every time politics comes up.
senses.exampleCN: 一谈到政治，我叔叔就变成了爱说教的人。
senses.why: The verb lecture also means to scold, so the personality sense of the -er noun carries that critical tone.
senses.whyCN: 动词 lecture 还有「训斥、说教」之义，这一引申义使「爱教训别人的人」成为义项。

intro.en: Lecturer is English lecture plus the person-forming suffix -er, and lecture goes back to Latin legere, to read.
intro.cn: lecturer 由英语 lecture 加表人后缀 -er 构成，而 lecture 可追溯至拉丁语 legere（阅读）。

items.en: Legere means to gather, to pick out, and then to read.
items.cn: legere 原义为采集、挑出，后来引申为阅读。

items.en: Lectura is the act of reading, especially reading aloud from a text.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语 lectura 指阅读行为，尤指出声朗读文本。

items.en: Lecture means a reading or an academic talk read aloud in class.
items.cn: lecture 指一次阅读，或在课堂上朗读的学术讲授。

items.en: Lecture enters English as a reading and a formal lesson.
items.cn: lecture 进入英语，表示阅读与正式课业。

items.en: The verb lecture develops, and lecturer appears as the person who lectures.
items.cn: 动词 lecture 发展成型，lecturer 随之出现，指讲课的人。

items.en: Lecturer becomes a standard British academic rank.
items.cn: lecturer 在英国固定为一个标准的学术职级。

note.en: Lecturer sits in the read-and-talk family of lecture, lection, and lectern, and beside teacher words such as tutor and professor.
note.cn: lecturer 属于 lecture、lection、lectern 这一「阅读与讲说」词族，并与 tutor、professor 等教师词相邻。

entries.definition: a formal talk given to teach or inform
entries.definitionCN: 讲座；课程讲授

entries.definition: the post or work of a lecturer
entries.definitionCN: 讲师职位

entries.definition: a stand holding a book for a speaker to read
entries.definitionCN: 讲台；读经台

entries.definition: a teacher who works with small groups or one student
entries.definitionCN: 辅导教师；导师

entries.definition: the senior rank of university teacher
entries.definitionCN: 教授

entries.definition: someone who gives a speech to an audience
entries.definitionCN: 演讲者；发言者

normalIntro.en: Lecturer is the doer of lecture: someone whose work is to read, talk, and teach in front of a room.
normalIntro.cn: lecturer 是 lecture 的执行者：一个以读、讲、教为工作的人。

normal.en: The suffix -er turns a verb into a person: lecture becomes lecturer.
normal.cn: 后缀 -er 把动词变为人：lecture 加 -er 就是 lecturer。

normal.en: Latin legere means to read, and a lecture is the reading aloud of a text.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为阅读，讲座原本就是朗读文本。

normal.en: In British use, lecturer names a rank below professor.
normal.cn: 英式用法里，lecturer 是低于教授的职级名称。

normal.en: A lectern is the stand the lecturer reads from, so both share lect-.
normal.cn: lectern 是讲师读稿的讲台，两者共享 lect- 词根。

normal.en: To lecture someone can mean to scold, so a lecturer may sound like a preacher.
normal.cn: lecture 作动词还可表示训斥，所以 lecturer 有时带有说教味。

abstract.en: See a figure at the lectern holding a page and looking over the class.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在讲台后，拿着纸页抬眼扫视课堂。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden sign with lecturer written on a university office door.
abstract.cn: 想象大学办公室里一扇门上钉着写着 lecturer 的木牌。

abstract.en: Hear a guest voice arriving for one special talk and then leaving.
abstract.cn: 想象一个客串的声音为某场专题讲座而来，讲完就离开。

examples.en: The lecturer explained the results of the experiment to the class.
examples.cn: 讲师向全班讲解了实验的结果。

examples.en: My economics lecturer is also a researcher on inflation.
examples.cn: 我的经济学讲师同时也是研究通货膨胀的学者。

examples.en: Our department invited a guest lecturer to speak about medieval music.
examples.cn: 我们系邀请了一位客座讲者来谈中世纪音乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来客车」——讲课的人站在讲台上，如同在台上摆车展般念稿，这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 legere（阅读、挑读）→ 中古拉丁语 lectura（阅读）→ 古法语 lecture（朗读、讲授）→ 英语 lecture（讲座）+ -er（表人）→ lecturer，核心义「朗读讲述的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Lecturer starts with the simple doer sense, fixes into the British job title, widens to guest speakers, and finally takes on the tone of a long sermon.
sensesIntro.cn: lecturer 由「讲课的人」这一简单施动义出发，固化为英国职称，扩展到客座讲者，最后带上冗长说教的色彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a lectern reading a text aloud to a room of listeners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在讲台后，对着满屋听众出声朗读。

branches.en: The plain doer sense: the person who gives the talk.
branches.cn: 最基础的施动义：站在前面讲授的人。

branches.en: The rank sense grows when lecturing becomes a paid job.
branches.cn: 当讲授成为有薪工作，施动者就固化为职位名称。

branches.en: The guest sense widens the role to invited speakers.
branches.cn: 客座义把身份范围扩展到被邀请的讲者。

branches.en: Both the role and the rank share the same workplace image.
branches.cn: 身份义与职级义共享同一个教室意象。

branches.en: A long talk to an audience and a long scolding share the same lecturing voice.
branches.cn: 对听众的长篇讲授与长篇训斥共享同一种说教语气。

intro.en: Lecturer is built from the noun lecture and the native suffix -er, with related words lectern, lectureship, and lecturing sharing the same read-and-talk stem.
intro.cn: lecturer 由名词 lecture 加本族后缀 -er 构成，lectern、lectureship、lecturing 同属这一「阅读与讲说」词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere means to gather and to read, and its participle lectus plus the noun lectio supply the lect- stem of lecture and lecturer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为采集与阅读，其分词 lectus 与名词 lectio 提供 lecture 与 lecturer 的 lect- 词干。

items.meaning: to gather, to pick out, to read
items.example: Legere lies at the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: legere 是整个词族的根。

items.example: Lectus gives the lect- stem.
items.exampleCN: lectus 提供 lect- 词干。

items.example: Lectura travels into Old French as lecture.
items.exampleCN: lectura 传入古法语变为 lecture。

items.meaning: a talk given to teach; to give such a talk
items.example: Lecture is the base word of lecturer.
items.exampleCN: lecture 是 lecturer 的基础词。

items.meaning: a person who does an action
items.example: The suffix -er turns lecture into lecturer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 lecture 变成 lecturer。

items.example: Lecturer marks the doer clearly.
items.exampleCN: lecturer 清楚地标出施动者。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或职位的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ship forms lectureship.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ship 构成 lectureship。

items.example: Lectureship is the post, lecturer is the person.
items.exampleCN: lectureship 是职位，lecturer 是人。

items.example: Lectern keeps the reading image of legere.
items.exampleCN: lectern 保留了 legere 的阅读意象。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms lecturing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 lecturing。

definition_zh: 壁架；突出边缘；岩架；暗礁
definition_en: a narrow flat shelf that sticks out from a wall, a cliff, or a rock face
core_image: 鸟落在悬崖侧面伸出的一条窄石条上
scene: 登山者贴着岩壁横移，脚下只有一脚宽的通道。He edged along the ledge, keeping both hands flat against the rock above him.
sceneCN: 这里 ledge 是「壁架」（第 1 个义项：从墙面或岩壁横向伸出的窄平台）；句意：他紧贴着岩架侧身挪动，两只手平按在头顶的岩石上。

pos.zh: 壁架；突出边缘；岩架；暗礁

derivatives.zh: 意义相近的独立词，指「搁板材料；搁架系统」，与 ledge 无构词关系
意义相近的独立词，指「窗台；门槛」，可与 window ledge 换用
意义相近的独立词，指「礁石」，与暗礁义的 ledge 属于同一义场

senses.title: A shelf sticking out from a wall or cliff
senses.definition: a narrow flat piece that juts out from a vertical surface and can hold or support something
senses.definitionCN: 从竖直表面横向伸出、可以承托物品的窄平面
senses.example: A row of candles stood on the stone ledge above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门上方石制的壁架上摆着一排蜡烛。
senses.why: The word began as a shelf fixed to a wall, and that flat horizontal image is the core of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指固定在墙上的搁板，而「横向伸出的窄平面」正是后来各个义项的共同核心。

senses.title: A natural rock shelf on a slope
senses.definition: a narrow step of rock that stands out on the face of a mountain or a hillside
senses.definitionCN: 山体或山坡侧面伸出的窄石台
senses.example: The rescuers lowered a rope to the climbers trapped on the ledge.
senses.exampleCN: 救援者把绳索放给困在岩架上的登山者。
senses.why: Mountains present the same shelf shape in stone, so the wall image transfers directly to rock.
senses.whyCN: 山体在石头里呈现同一种「搁板」形状，于是墙面意象直接转移到岩石上。

senses.title: A projecting rim or edge
senses.definition: an edge that projects outward, as along the top of a tank, a frame, or a machine part
senses.definitionCN: 向外凸出的边缘，如水箱、框子或机械零件的沿口
senses.example: Water spilled over the ledge of the old bathtub.
senses.exampleCN: 水从旧浴缸的沿口溢了出来。
senses.why: Any narrow outward step can be called a ledge, so the noun also names the rim of a container or structure.
senses.whyCN: 任何窄小的外凸台阶都可称为 ledge，因此这个词也用来指容器或结构的沿口。

senses.title: A ridge of rock near the sea
senses.definition: a ridge of rock under or near the water that can make navigation dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 位于水下或近水处、会使航行危险的礁脊
senses.example: The fishing boat struck a ledge of rock about a mile offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船在离岸约一英里处撞上了一道礁脊。
senses.why: In nautical use the rock step sense narrows to a line of rock at sea level.
senses.whyCN: 在航海用法中，「岩石台阶」义收窄为海面附近的岩石脊线。

senses.title: A narrow shelf of land
senses.definition: a long narrow strip of higher ground running along a coast or hillside
senses.definitionCN: 沿海岸或山坡延伸的狭长高起地带
senses.example: Villagers built their huts on a grassy ledge above the river.
senses.exampleCN: 村民把棚屋建在河上方一片长草的台地上。
senses.why: The shelf shape also scales up to landforms, where it means a narrow terrace rather than a singular stone.
senses.whyCN: 「搁板」的形状也放大到地形层面，切指一条狭长的台地，而非单块石头。

intro.en: Ledge is a Middle English word for a bar or a shelf, generally related to the verb to lay and to the noun layer.
intro.cn: ledge 是中古英语词，义为横条或搁板，一般认为与动词 lay 及名词 layer 同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root ledh- is thought to mean a crossbar or a ridge.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 ledh- 表示横木或凸起的条脊。

items.en: Legge means a bar, a ridge, or the wooden crossbar of a fishing weir.
items.cn: 中古英语 legge 指横木、脊条，或鱼梁上的木横条。

items.en: The sense widens to any narrow shelf that projects from a surface.
items.cn: 该词义扩展为任何从表面向外伸出的窄搁板。

items.en: The word is written as ledge and covers rock shelves on cliffs.
items.cn: 词形固定为 ledge，并开始指悬崖上的岩石平台。

items.en: Sailors and surveyors apply ledge to rocks and strips of land.
items.cn: 航海者与测量员把 ledge 用于礁石与狭长地块。

items.en: The general shelf sense is now rare, and rock and window ledges dominate.
items.cn: 现今通用的搁板义已少见，岩石壁架与窗台成为主要用法。

note.en: Ledge belongs to the narrow shelf family with sill, shelf, and banister rubrails, and sits beside cliff and reef words in meaning.
note.cn: ledge 与 sill、shelf 等同属「窄搁板」词族，在意义上则与悬崖、礁石类词相邻。

entries.definition: a book in which money records are kept
entries.definitionCN: 总账；账簿；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a vehicle that runs on runners over snow
entries.definitionCN: 雪橇；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a serious promise or a security given for a loan
entries.definitionCN: 保证；抵押；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the flat bottom part of a window or doorway
entries.definitionCN: 窗台；门槛

entries.definition: a flat board fixed to a wall for holding things
entries.definitionCN: 搁板；架子

entries.definition: a line of rocks just above or below the sea surface
entries.definitionCN: 礁石

normalIntro.en: Ledge is a thin shelf pushed out of a wall: narrow, flat, and only wide enough for a few things.
normalIntro.cn: ledge 是从墙里推出的一条薄搁板：窄、平，只够放几样东西。

normal.en: The word is related to to lay and to layer: something laid along a wall.
normal.cn: ledge 与 lay、layer 同源，本义是沿墙铺开的东西。

normal.en: Window ledge is a set phrase for the indoor sill of a window.
normal.cn: window ledge 是固定说法，指窗户内侧的窗台。

normal.en: Keep the hard g sound /dʒ/, so ledge rhymes with edge and hedge.
normal.cn: 注意发硬颚音 /dʒ/，ledge 与 edge、hedge 押韵。

normal.en: Climbers speak of a rest ledge as a small safe stop on a long route.
normal.cn: 登山者把路线上的小休息平台称为 rest ledge。

normal.en: Do not confuse ledge with ledger, the account book, which has another history.
normal.cn: 别把 ledge 记成 ledger（账簿），两者的来历不同。

abstract.en: Picture a candle tray fixed neatly under a window frame.
abstract.cn: 想象在窗框下沿齐整地装了一条放蜡烛的托板。

abstract.en: See a goat standing on a white rock step halfway up a cliff.
abstract.cn: 想象一只山羊站在悬崖半腰的一道白色石阶上。

abstract.en: Feel the sharp lip of a full water tank against your hand.
abstract.cn: 回想装满水的水箱边沿抵在手上的锐利触感。

examples.en: A cat sat on the wide ledge of the kitchen window.
examples.cn: 一只猫坐在厨房窗台宽阔的窗沿上。

examples.en: The hikers rested on a narrow ledge cut into the mountain.
examples.cn: 徒步者在山体上开凿出的窄岩架上休息。

examples.en: Seagulls nest on the rocky ledges of the island.
examples.cn: 海鸥在岛上多岩石的壁架上筑巢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莱吉」——读起来像往墙上一「垒」出一块平放的搁板，这只是谐音联想，并非真实词源。

root: 一般认为与古英语 lecgan（放置）同源，中古英语 legge（横木、脊条）→ ledge（壁架、搁板），核心义「横向伸出的窄平面」；词根存疑处已标注。

sensesIntro.en: Ledge begins with a shelf on a wall, spreads to rock faces and rims, narrows to reef lines and land terraces in specialist use.
sensesIntro.cn: ledge 从墙上的搁板起步，扩展到岩壁与沿口，又在专业用法中收窄为礁脊与台地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow flat shelf pushed out from a wall or a cliff.
core.cn: 核心意象：从墙面或崖壁向外推出的一条窄平搁板。

branches.en: The man-made shelf is the original sense.
branches.cn: 人造搁板是这个词的本义。

branches.en: Stone versions of the same shelf shape give the climbing sense.
branches.cn: 石头版本的同一种搁板形状，形成攀登语境中的义项。

branches.en: Any outward rim keeps the projecting edge idea.
branches.cn: 任何外凸的沿口都保留「凸出边缘」的意象。

branches.en: Rock shelves in mountains and ridges in the sea share the stone-step image.
branches.cn: 山上的岩架与海中的礁脊共享「石台阶」意象。

branches.en: The narrow shelf scales up into a strip of land along a coast.
branches.cn: 窄搁板的形状被放大，成为沿海的一条狭长地带。

intro.en: Ledge is an English word with a Germanic base, related to lay and layer; its later companions are the shortened form ledge and the technical noun ledged.
intro.cn: ledge 是带日耳曼语根基的英语词，与 lay、layer 相关；此后又出现 ledged 等技术性派生用法。

latinIntro.en: Ledge has no Latin source, so the entries below compare it with the unrelated Latin roots that gave its companion words.
latinIntro.cn: ledge 并非来自拉丁语，下列条目仅用于对照那些带来相关词的拉丁语词根。

items.example: Lecgan is the ancient relative of ledge.
items.exampleCN: lecgan 是 ledge 的古老同源词。

items.example: Legge is the direct Middle English ancestor.
items.exampleCN: legge 是中古英语中的直接祖形。

items.meaning: a thickness of material laid over a surface
items.example: Layer keeps the same laying image.
items.exampleCN: layer 保留同样的「铺设」意象。

items.example: Ledge is the modern standard form.
items.exampleCN: ledge 是现代标准词形。

items.example: Ledger looks close to ledge but has another history.
items.exampleCN: ledger 看似与 ledge 相近，但来历不同。

items.meaningCN: 加在名词后表示「具有某物」
items.example: A ledged door has rails fixed across it.
items.exampleCN: ledged door 指装有横条的门。

items.meaning: an opening in a wall fitted with glass
items.example: Window and ledge form the set phrase window ledge.
items.exampleCN: window 与 ledge 组成固定搭配 window ledge。

items.example: Rock and ledge pair to describe cliff surfaces.
items.exampleCN: rock 与 ledge 常搭配描述悬崖表面。

items.meaning: a rock step used by climbers
items.example: Climbing guides mark every usable ledge on a route.
items.exampleCN: 攀岩指南会标出路线上的每一处可落脚岩架。

definition_zh: 韭葱；青蒜；威尔士的国徽标志
definition_en: a long green vegetable of the onion family, with a thick white base and flat folded leaves
core_image: 一把茎白叶绿的韭葱立在一篮蔬菜中间
scene: 炖锅已经在炉子上冒热气，食材还差最后一样。She peeled the outer layer off a leek and sliced the pale base into the soup.
sceneCN: 这里 leek 是「韭葱」（第 1 个义项：葱属的一种长条蔬菜）；句意：她剥掉韭葱外面的一层，把颜色浅的根部切进汤里。

collocations.zh: 韭葱与水仙（威尔士的两个标志）

derivatives.zh: 同出古英语 leac 这一葱韭词根，由 gar（矛）加 leac 构成，指「大蒜」
leek 加 house 构成的复合词，指长在屋顶上的「瓦松」

senses.title: The long green vegetable
senses.definition: a tall vegetable of the onion group whose leaves are folded flat and whose base is white and sweet
senses.definitionCN: 葱属的一种高棵蔬菜，叶片是扁平的折叶，根部发白、味道偏甜
senses.example: The market sells leeks, onions, and apples every Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 这个集市每逢周六出售韭葱、洋葱和苹果。
senses.why: The old English leac was a general word for the leek plant, and the modern word kept that everyday food sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 leac 本来就是指葱韭类植物的通称，现代词保留了这类日常蔬菜义。

senses.title: The white base used in cooking
senses.definition: the soft pale lower part that is washed, sliced, and cooked in soups and stews
senses.definitionCN: 柔软色浅的下半段，洗净切片后用于汤和炖菜
senses.example: Wash the leek carefully, since grit often hides between the outer layers.
senses.exampleCN: 要仔细洗净韭葱，因为泥沙常藏在层叶之间。
senses.why: Cooks treat the base as a separate ingredient, so the plant and its usable stem part became two practical senses.
senses.whyCN: 厨师把根部当作单独的食材对待，于是「整棵植物」与「可食用根部」成了两个实用意义。

senses.title: The national emblem of Wales
senses.definition: a plant worn on Saint David Day to show Welsh identity
senses.definitionCN: 在圣大卫节佩戴以表示威尔士身份的一种植物
senses.example: Many visitors pin a leek to their coat on the first of March.
senses.exampleCN: 许多游客在三月一日把韭葱别在外套上。
senses.why: Legends tie the leek to a Welsh battlefield, and the plant became a national badge instead of merely food.
senses.whyCN: 传说把韭葱与威尔士的一场战役联系起来，这株植物就从食物变成了民族徽记。

senses.title: Garlic, in older use
senses.definition: the older English word for garlic, now kept only in old texts
senses.definitionCN: 大蒜的古英语叫法，如今只见于旧文献
senses.example: Old recipes in the collection still use leek where we would say garlic.
senses.exampleCN: 这本题集中的旧食谱仍用 leek 表示我们今天所说的 garlic。
senses.why: Because leac covered onion-like plants in general, it once also meant garlic, before garlic took that place.
senses.whyCN: 由于 leac 泛指葱蒜类，它也曾用来指大蒜，后来才由 garlic 专管。

intro.en: Leek comes from Old English leac, an ancient Germanic word for plants of the onion group.
intro.cn: leek 来自古英语 leac，是日耳曼语中表示葱蒜类植物的古老词。

items.en: A reconstructed root laukaz names the onion and leek plants.
items.cn: 重构词根 laukaz 指洋葱与韭葱一类植物。

items.en: Leac means a leek or any strong onion-like vegetable.
items.cn: 古英语 leac 指韭葱或任何气味浓烈的葱蒜类蔬菜。

items.en: The forms leek and leke settle as the name for the garden leek.
items.cn: leek、leke 等写法稳定下来，专指园栽韭葱。

items.en: Garlic replaces the leek-like old word for garlic, and leek narrows to one plant.
items.cn: garlic 取代了旧词的大蒜义，leek 收窄为一种植物。

items.en: The leek stands beside the daffodil as a Welsh national sign.
items.cn: 韭葱与水仙并列为威尔士的民族标志。

items.en: Leek is now mainly a cooking word plus a cultural emblem.
items.cn: 如今 leek 主要是烹饪词汇，并兼作文化徽记。

note.en: Leek sits inside the onion family with garlic, chive, and shallot, and has near-twins in the kitchen: onion and spring onion.
note.cn: leek 与 garlic、chive、shallot 同属葱韭词族，在厨房里则与 onion、spring onion 互为近邻。

entries.definition: a strong-smelling bulb made of small cloves
entries.definitionCN: 大蒜，与 leek 同出葱韭词根

entries.definition: a succulent plant that grows on roofs and walls
entries.definitionCN: 瓦松，长在屋顶或墙上，词形里带 leek

entries.definition: a hole that lets liquid or gas escape
entries.definitionCN: 泄漏；只是读音相同、拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a round bulb with many layers and a sharp taste
entries.definitionCN: 洋葱

entries.definition: a small young onion eaten with its green tops
entries.definitionCN: 小葱；青葱

entries.definition: a thin hollow green leaf of the onion family
entries.definitionCN: 细香葱

normalIntro.en: Leek is the tall polite cousin of the onion: white at the foot, green at the head, and full of earthy sweetness.
normalIntro.cn: leek 是洋葱温和的高个子亲戚：脚下发白、顶上发绿，带土味的清甜。

normal.en: Old English leac was the general word for leeks and garlic alike.
normal.cn: 古英语 leac 是韭葱与大蒜的共同通称。

normal.en: Garlic is the compound of gar and leac, so the two words are cousins.
normal.cn: garlic 由 gar 与 leac 复合而成，两词是近亲。

normal.en: Say the long vowel /iː/, so leek rhymes with peek and seek.
normal.cn: 注意发长元音 /iː/，leek 与 peek、seek 押韵。

normal.en: Keep it apart from leak, the hole that lets water out.
normal.cn: 要与 leak（漏水处）分清楚。

normal.en: In Wales the leek and the daffodil are worn on the national day.
normal.cn: 在威尔士，国庆时会佩戴韭葱与水仙。

abstract.en: See a bundle of pale green stems standing upright in a basket.
abstract.cn: 想象一捆淡绿色茎秆直立在提篮里。

abstract.en: Picture the clean white base sliding under a knife on a chopping board.
abstract.cn: 想象发白的根部在砧板上滑到刀下被切开。

abstract.en: Hear fabric rustle as a green leek badge is pinned to a coat.
abstract.cn: 想象把绿色韭葱徽章别到外套上时布料的轻响。

examples.en: The chef washed three leeks and cut them into thin rings.
examples.cn: 厨师洗净三根韭葱，切成细圈。

examples.en: Potato and leek soup is a favourite in winter.
examples.cn: 土豆韭葱汤是冬天很受欢迎的一道汤。

examples.en: He wore a leek on his jacket for the Welsh national day.
examples.cn: 他在威尔士国庆日把一株韭葱别在夹克上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立刻」——汤要「立刻」好喝，就丢一把韭葱进去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 leac（葱韭类）→ 中古英语 leek / leke → 现代英语 leek，核心义「一种长形的葱属蔬菜」；同源词包括 garlic、houseleek。

sensesIntro.en: Leek starts as the whole plant, narrows to the edible stem, widens to a Welsh emblem, and keeps an old sense of garlic.
sensesIntro.cn: leek 先指整株植物，再收窄到可食用的茎部，扩展到威尔士徽记，还保留一个指「大蒜」的古义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall stem that is white at the foot and green at the head, standing in a basket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根下白上绿的高茎蔬菜立在篮子里。

branches.en: The whole plant is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 整株植物是日常义。

branches.en: Cooks meet the plant as a pale stem to slice.
branches.cn: 厨师接触的是要切片的那段浅色茎。

branches.en: A plant worn on the coat becomes a national sign.
branches.cn: 植物被别在外套上，就成了民族标志。

branches.en: The old wide meaning once covered garlic too.
branches.cn: 旧时的宽泛意义也曾覆盖大蒜。

branches.en: The whole plant and its base are the same thing at two levels.
branches.cn: 整株植物与根部是同一事物的两个层面。

intro.en: Leek is a native English word from leac, with garlic and houseleek as its best-known relatives and no added prefixes or suffixes.
intro.cn: leek 是源自 leac 的本族英语词，最知名的亲属是 garlic 与 houseleek，本身没有附加前缀或后缀。

latinIntro.en: Leek is Germanic in origin, not Latin, so the entries below note only the Latin names that naturalists later used for it.
latinIntro.cn: leek 源自日耳曼语而非拉丁语，下列条目仅记录博物学家后来为它使用的拉丁名。

items.example: Laukaz is the reconstructed ancestor of leek.
items.exampleCN: laukaz 是 leek 的重构祖形。

items.example: Leac is the direct Old English source.
items.exampleCN: leac 是直接的古英语来源。

items.example: Leek narrows to one kitchen plant.
items.exampleCN: leek 收窄为一种厨房植物。

items.example: Gar plus leac makes the old name of garlic.
items.exampleCN: gar 加 leac 构成大蒜的旧称。

items.meaning: spear leek, now the garlic bulb
items.meaningCN: 原指矛形韭葱，现指大蒜
items.example: Garlic shares the leek root.
items.exampleCN: garlic 共享韭葱词根。

items.example: House plus leek names a roof plant.
items.exampleCN: house 加 leek 指一种屋顶植物。

items.example: Houseleek is not a leek at all in the kitchen sense.
items.exampleCN: houseleek 在厨房意义上完全不是韭葱。

items.meaning: to remove an outer skin or layer
items.example: Cooks peel off the tough outer leaves of a leek.
items.exampleCN: 厨师会剥掉韭葱外层的粗叶。

latinEntries.example: Modern botany names the leek Allium porrum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 现代植物学把韭葱定名为 Allium porrum。

latinEntries.example: Porrum is the old Latin name for the leek.
latinEntries.exampleCN: porrum 是韭葱的古老拉丁名。

definition_zh: 遗产；遗赠物；遗留问题；传承；软件旧版
definition_en: money or property left to someone in a will, or a long lasting effect or problem handed down from the past
core_image: 一只旧木箱换了主人：箱子上还贴着上任主人写的名字，里面的东西照旧交给后来的人
scene: 老人去世后，律师当众念遗嘱，把庭院里那棵苹果树连同园子一起交给孙子。After the old man died, the lawyer read the will aloud and handed the apple tree in the courtyard and the garden to his grandson as a legacy.
sceneCN: 这里 legacy 是「遗产、遗赠物」（第 1 个义项：遗嘱中留给别人的钱或财物）；句意：老人去世后，律师当众念遗嘱，把庭院里的苹果树连同园子作为遗产交给孙子。

pos.zh: 旧式的；过时但仍在使用（尤指电脑系统）

derivatives.zh: 由 legacy 与中古法语词尾组合而成，义为「受遗赠人」
由拉丁语 legare 直接进入英语，义为「遗赠；遗留给他人」
由 legate 加 -ion 构成，义为「使团；公使馆」，词根仍是「派遣、委任」

senses.title: Money or property left in a will
senses.definition: money or property that someone leaves to another person when they die
senses.definitionCN: 某人在去世时留给别人的钱或财物
senses.example: Her aunt left her a small legacy of books and furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 她的姑妈留给她一小笔由书和家具组成的遗产。
senses.why: The Latin base legare means to appoint or hand over by will, so the box of property passed on at death is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 legare 意为「嘱托、以遗嘱交付」，所以在人去世时交接的那一箱财物是最早的义项。

senses.title: A long lasting effect passed on to later generations
senses.definition: an effect, idea, or institution that continues to exist after its originator has gone
senses.definitionCN: 某个事物在最初的人或事件之后仍继续存在的影响、观念或制度
senses.example: The festival is part of the legacy that the settlers left to the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日是移民者留给这座小镇的一份传承。
senses.why: Once the inheritance image is loosened, what is handed on need not be money, and a habit or an idea can be the thing in the old box.
senses.whyCN: 把「继承」的画面放宽之后，交接下去的不必是钱，一种习惯或一个观念也可以放进那只旧木箱。

senses.title: A problem or burden inherited from the past
senses.definition: an inherited situation, often unwelcome, that later people have to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 后人不得不处理的继承而来的状况，多含不受欢迎之意
senses.example: The new council inherited a legacy of debt and broken roads.
senses.exampleCN: 新一届议会接手了一堆债务和坏路的遗留问题。
senses.why: A legacy is not always welcome, and the same imagery that hands on a gift can also hand on a problem nobody chose.
senses.whyCN: 遗产并不总是受欢迎的，交接礼物的同一幅画面也能交接一个人并没有选择的麻烦。

senses.title: An outdated but still used computer system
senses.definition: an old computer system or program kept in operation because newer ones are costly to adopt
senses.definitionCN: 因为更换新系统代价高而仍在运转的旧电脑系统或旧程序
senses.example: The bank still runs the payroll on a legacy system.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行仍在一套旧版系统上运行工资发放。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word for what is inherited from the past generation, so an old program still in use is a legacy from an earlier era.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了这个词来指上一代留下来的东西，因此仍在使用的旧程序就是上一个年代的遗留物。

intro.en: Legacy comes from Latin legare, to appoint or bequeath, through Medieval Latin legatia and Old French legacie.
intro.cn: legacy 来自拉丁语 legare（委任、遗赠），经中世纪拉丁语 legatia 与古法语 legacie 进入英语。

items.en: Legare means to send with a commission, to bequeath, or to appoint.
items.cn: legare 意为委派、遗赠或任命。

items.en: Legatia names the office of a legate, someone sent with a charge.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 legatia 指使节的职务，即使者被委以任务。

items.en: Legacie means the office of a deputy and then a bequest.
items.cn: 古法语 legacie 先指代表者的职务，再指遗赠。

items.en: Lawyers used the word for property left under a will.
items.cn: 法学家用这个词指依遗嘱留下的财物。

items.en: Late Middle English legacy first means a body of legates, then a bequest.
items.cn: 中古英语后期的 legacy 先指使团，后指遗赠物。

items.en: The word widens to mean anything handed down, including old software.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义扩大为任何流传下来的东西，包括旧软件。

note.en: Legacy is close in spelling to legate, delegation, and legacy words such as heritage and inheritance.
note.cn: legacy 与 legate、delegation 拼写相近，也与 heritage、inheritance 等表示「传承」的词相邻。

entries.definition: an official envoy sent with a special charge
entries.definitionCN: 受特殊委任派出的正式使节，与 legacy 同出拉丁语 legare

entries.definition: a group of people sent to represent others
entries.definitionCN: 代表团；派出的代表，与 legacy 共享「委派」词根

entries.definition: the plural of legacy
entries.definitionCN: legacy 的复数形式，词义不变

entries.definition: traditions and buildings valued as the product of earlier generations
entries.definitionCN: 世代相传并被视为名分的传统与建筑；偏重集体文化

entries.definition: money or property received from someone who has died
entries.definitionCN: 继承所得的钱财；偏重依法继承本身

entries.definition: a gift of property made in a will
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱中的遗赠；最正式，限于法律文本

normalIntro.en: Legacy is the inheritance image: whatever an earlier generation hands over, either as gift or as burden.
normalIntro.cn: legacy 的核心是「交接」：上一代留下的东西，无论是礼物还是负担。

normal.en: Leave a legacy means to give something that outlives you.
normal.cn: leave a legacy 意为留下比生命更长久的東西。

normal.en: Compare heritage and inheritance: legacy can be either a gift or a burden.
normal.cn: 对比 heritage 与 inheritance：legacy 既可指礼物，也可指负担。

normal.en: A legacy system is old software still in use, not a system about wills.
normal.cn: legacy system 指仍在使用的旧软件，与遗嘱无关。

normal.en: The plural is legacies, spelled with ies after a consonant.
normal.cn: 复数写作 legacies，辅音字母后改 y 为 ies。

normal.en: The root legare means to bequeath, so legatee is the person who receives.
normal.cn: 词根 legare 意为遗赠，所以 legatee 指接受遗赠的人。

abstract.en: Picture an old wooden box changing hands at a funeral.
abstract.cn: 想象一只旧木箱在葬礼上换了主人。

abstract.en: Think of a tree a settler planted that still shades the town square.
abstract.cn: 想象移民者种下的一棵树，至今仍为镇广场遮阴。

abstract.en: See a dusty bill nobody chose to pay, passed down desk to desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一张没人愿意付的旧账单，在办公桌之间一代代往下传。

examples.en: The artist left a lasting legacy of paintings to the city.
examples.cn: 这位画家给城市留下了持久的绘画遗产。

examples.en: Poverty is one legacy of the long war.
examples.cn: 贫困是那场漫长战争留下的遗留问题之一。

examples.en: Engineers are slowly replacing the legacy software.
examples.cn: 工程师们正在慢慢替换那套旧版软件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累给斯」——上辈「累」着「给」下去的东西，就是你继承的遗产；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 legare（委任；遗赠）→ 中世纪拉丁语 legatia（使节的职务）→ 古法语 legacie（遗赠）→ 中古英语 legacy（使团；遗赠物）→ 现代英语 legacy（遗产；传承；遗留问题），核心义「交由后来者接手」。

sensesIntro.en: Legacy starts as money left in a will, widens to any effect a generation passes on, then to an inherited problem, and finally to old technology still in use.
sensesIntro.cn: legacy 先指遗嘱里留下的钱财，再扩大到一代人交给下一代的一切影响，然后是继承来的麻烦，最后指仍在使用的旧技术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old wooden box handed to the next owner with the old name still on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只贴着旧名字的旧木箱交到下一位主人手里。

branches.en: The will and its property is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 遗嘱与其中的财物是字面义项。

branches.en: What is passed on can be an idea or a tradition.
branches.cn: 被交接的也可以是一种观念或传统。

branches.en: The same handover can carry debt and damage.
branches.cn: 同一种交接也可能带来债务与破坏。

branches.en: Money and influence alike are things a person leaves behind.
branches.cn: 钱财与影响都是一个人身后留下的东西。

branches.en: A burden and an old system are both left over from an earlier era.
branches.cn: 历史包袱与旧版系统都是上一个年代残留下来的东西。

intro.en: Legacy is built on the Latin root leg-, to send or appoint, which also gives legate, delegate, and legation.
intro.cn: legacy 建立在拉丁语词根 leg-（派遣、委任）之上，lege、legate、delegate 与 legation 都出自同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin legare means to appoint, delegate, or bequeath, and legatum is a thing bequeathed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legare 意为委任、派遣或遗赠，legatum 指被遗赠之物。

items.example: Legare gives the handing over image.
items.exampleCN: legare 提供「交接托付」的意象。

items.example: Legatum is the item left behind.
items.exampleCN: legatum 指留下的东西。

items.example: The French form carries both meanings.
items.exampleCN: 法语形式兼具两种含义。

items.example: A legate is sent with a charge.
items.exampleCN: 使节带着任务被派出。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态、职务或身份的后缀
items.example: The suffix -acy appears in legacy and accuracy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -acy 见于 legacy 与 accuracy。

items.example: Legacies keeps the noun sense.
items.exampleCN: legacies 保留名词含义。

items.meaning: a person who receives a bequest
items.example: The legatee signed the papers.
items.exampleCN: 受遗赠人签署了文件。

items.example: Delegate shares the latin root of sending.
items.exampleCN: delegate 共享拉丁语「派遣」词根。

items.example: Legation keeps the office sense.
items.exampleCN: legation 保留「职务」含义。

definition_zh: 传说中的；传奇的；极有名的；非同凡响的
definition_en: described in old stories that may not be true, extremely famous, or so remarkable that the story sounds unlikely
core_image: 篝火边的老人指着夜空，把很久以前的一位英雄讲给围坐的孩子听
scene: 篝火旁，老人对围坐的孩子们讲一位拔剑立誓的国王，孩子们听得入迷。By the campfire, the old man told the children about a legendary king who drew his sword and swore an oath.
sceneCN: 这里 legendary 是「传说中的」（第 1 个义项：只出现在古老故事里、未必真实存在）；句意：篝火旁，老人对围坐的孩子们讲一位拔剑立誓的传说国王。

pos.zh: 非同凡响的；令人难以置信的

derivatives.zh: 去词尾 -ary 得到的基础名词，义为「传说；传奇人物」
由 legendary 加 -ly 构成，义为「传奇般地」
由 legend 加 -ry 构成，义为「传说文学；传奇传说集」

senses.title: Described in old stories that may not be true
senses.definition: told about in traditional stories whose facts cannot be checked
senses.definitionCN: 在传统故事中被讲述、其事实无法核实的
senses.example: The legendary city was said to rest on golden pillars.
senses.exampleCN: 据说那座传说中的城市建在金色的柱子上。
senses.why: Legenda in medieval Latin means things to be read, especially lives of saints, so legendary starts as belonging to such stories.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 legenda 意为「应当被诵读的东西」，尤指圣人传记，所以 legendary 最初就是「属于这类故事的」。

senses.title: Extremely famous and admired
senses.definition: so famous that people tell stories and rumours about them
senses.definitionCN: 名声极大，以至于人们会讲述关于他的故事和传闻
senses.example: The chef became legendary for her chili sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 这位厨师因她的辣椒酱而成为传奇。
senses.why: Once a person is talked about enough, the stories grow larger than the facts, and the word drifts from the story to the fame itself.
senses.whyCN: 一个人被谈论得足够多，故事就会长成比事实更大的样子，词义于是从「故事」滑向「名声」本身。

senses.title: Remarkable to the point of disbelief
senses.titleCN: 非同凡响的；令人难以置信的
senses.definition: so impressive or extreme that it seems hardly believable
senses.definitionCN: 出色或极端到让人几乎难以相信的
senses.example: His legendary patience outlasted three committees.
senses.exampleCN: 他那传奇般的耐心耗过了三个委员会。
senses.why: In lively speech legendary signals that something sounds too unlikely to be true, so it becomes a strong intensifier for excess.
senses.whyCN: 在口语里 legendary 常暗示某事听起来太不像真的，于是变成表示「过分」的强语气词。

intro.en: Legendary is formed from legend, which derives from Latin legenda, meaning things to be read, and from Medieval Latin legendarius.
intro.cn: legendary 由 legend 派生，而 legend 源于拉丁语 legenda（应当诵读的东西）与中世纪拉丁语 legendarius。

items.en: Legenda means things to be read, a neuter plural of legere, to read.
items.cn: 拉丁语 legenda 意为「应当诵读的东西」，是 legere（阅读）的中性复数形式。

items.en: Legenda aurea, the golden readings, collects the lives of saints.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 legenda aurea（黄金传说）收录了圣人传记。

items.en: Legende means a reading, a life of a saint, or a tale.
items.cn: 古法语 legende 意为诵读、圣人传记或故事。

items.en: English legend means a story of a saint, later any traditional tale.
items.cn: 英语 legend 先指圣人故事，后指任何传统故事。

items.en: Legendary appears for what is told in legends.
items.cn: legendary 出现，表示「在传说中被讲述的」。

items.en: The word widens to famous people and astonishing events.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义扩展到著名人物与惊人的事件。

note.en: Legendary shares its spelling and root with legend and legendry, and overlaps in meaning with mythic, iconic, and famous.
note.cn: legendary 与 legend、legendry 拼写和词根相同，在意义上与 mythic、iconic、famous 有重叠。

entries.definition: a traditional story, or a very famous person
entries.definitionCN: 传说故事或极有名的人物，去掉词尾即得 legendary

entries.definition: legends as a body of traditional literature
entries.definitionCN: 传说文学；传说集。只是拼写相近，与 legendary 词源同出 legend 但词性不同

entries.definition: clear enough to be read
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚的；可读的。只是拼写相近，词源与传说无关，来自阅读一词

entries.definition: existing only in ancient stories
entries.definitionCN: 仅存在于古代神话中的；偏重虚构的神话来源

entries.definition: widely admired as a much loved symbol
entries.definitionCN: 被公认为标志性偶像的；偏重象征意义

entries.definition: known by very many people
entries.definitionCN: 众所周知的；最中性，不含传奇色彩

normalIntro.en: Legendary is simply legend plus the adjective ending, so think of the story first and the fame second.
normalIntro.cn: legendary 就是 legend 加形容词词尾，先想「故事」，再想「名声」。

normal.en: Legend plus ary: the story in legend is what legendary describes.
normal.cn: legend 加 ary：legend 里的故事正是 legendary 所描述的。

normal.en: It rarely takes -er or -est; use more and most.
normal.cn: 它很少加 -er 或 -est，比较用 more 与 most。

normal.en: A legendary figure is a person whole generations tell stories about.
normal.cn: legendary figure 指被一代代人讲述故事的人。

normal.en: Compare that landmark with mythic, which points to gods and ancient myth.
normal.cn: 对比 mythic：后者偏向神明与古代神话。

normal.en: Legendary status is the state of having become more story than fact.
normal.cn: legendary status 指已经变成故事多过事实的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a fire, a pointing finger, and a wide night sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆篝火、一只指向前方的手和辽阔的夜空。

abstract.en: Imagine a signed poster on a stadium wall that fans queue to touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一张贴在体育场墙上的签名海报，球迷排着队去摸它。

abstract.en: See a chef lifting a pan in a cloud of fire, as if from a story.
abstract.cn: 想象一位厨师在火焰中端起炒锅，像是从故事里走出来。

examples.en: The legendary hero was said to be strong enough to move a mountain.
examples.cn: 据说那位传说中的英雄力大足以移山。

examples.en: Her legendary calm kept the whole team steady.
examples.cn: 她那传奇般的镇定让整个团队保持了稳定。

examples.en: The story has grown legendary among the villagers.
examples.cn: 这个故事在村民当中已经变成了传说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乐之传说」——听起来像一首让人快乐的传说，就是「传奇的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 legere（阅读）→ 中性复数 legenda（应当诵读的东西，尤指圣人传记）→ 中世纪拉丁语 legendarius → 古法语 legende → 英语 legend → 16 世纪英语 legendary（传说中的）→ 现代英语「传奇的；极有名的」。

sensesIntro.en: Legendary first describes the heroes of old stories, then people whose fame has grown story like, and finally anything so remarkable that it hardly seems true.
sensesIntro.cn: legendary 先描述旧故事里的英雄，再指名声已经像故事一样大的人，最后指好到几乎不像真的任何事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man at a fire pointing at the night sky while children listen.
core.cn: 核心意象：老人坐在火边，一边指着夜空一边讲，孩子们听得入神。

branches.en: The story sense is the oldest and most literal.
branches.cn: 「故事」义是最古老、最字面的义项。

branches.en: Fame grows out of the stories people retell.
branches.cn: 「名声」来自人们一遍遍重述的故事。

branches.en: Extreme degree borrows the disbelief of the tale.
branches.cn: 「极度」义借用了传说那种难以置信的感觉。

branches.en: A hero of old stories and a famous chef both reach the word by being told about.
branches.cn: 传说中的英雄与名厨都是靠被反复谈论才走到这个词上。

branches.en: To call something legendary is to say its scale has left the ordinary behind.
branches.cn: 称某事 legendary，等于说它的规模已经超出了寻常。

intro.en: Legendary is legend plus the adjective ending -ary, both of which go back to Latin legere, to read.
intro.cn: legendary 是 legend 加形容词词尾 -ary，两者都上溯到拉丁语 legere（阅读）。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere means to read or gather, legenda means things to be read, and legendarius means a book of legends.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为阅读、收集，legenda 意为应当诵读的东西，legendarius 意为传说集。

items.example: Legere gives the reading image behind legend.
items.exampleCN: legere 提供 legend 背后的「阅读」意象。

items.example: Legenda later named lives of saints.
items.exampleCN: legenda 后来专指圣人传记。

items.example: The legendarius was read aloud in church.
items.exampleCN: 传说集在当时被在教堂中朗读。

items.example: Legend is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: legend 是这个形容词背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ary changes legend into legendary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 把 legend 变成 legendary。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms legendarily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 legendarily。

items.example: The word legendarily modifies the verb.
items.exampleCN: legendarily 修饰动词。

items.example: Legendry book is one word shorter than legendary.
items.exampleCN: legendry 比 legendary 少一个元音。

items.example: Mythic is the nearest formal rival.
items.exampleCN: mythic 是最接近的正式对等词。

definition_zh: 合法性；正当性；合理性；婚生（身份）
definition_en: the quality of being allowed by law, accepted as right by people, or reasonable and fair
core_image: 一份文件被盖上红章，又被众人举手表决通过，最后摆上档案架
scene: 选举结束后，观察员逐一核对选票与登记册，确认新一届议会有权作出决定。After the election, the observers checked the ballot papers against the register to confirm the legitimacy of the new council.
sceneCN: 这里 legitimacy 是「合法性、正当性」（第 1 个义项：依法律与程序被认可的地位）；句意：选举结束后，观察员逐一核对选票与登记册，确认新一届议会的合法性。

pos.zh: 合法性；依法成立的资格

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -acy 得到的形容词，义为「合法的；正当的」
由 legitimate 加 -ize 构成，义为「使合法化；使正当化」
由前缀 il- 加 legitimacy 构成，义为「不合法；非婚生」

senses.title: The state of being allowed by law
senses.definition: the condition of being lawful or formally permitted by the law
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律而被许可或正式成立的状态
senses.example: The court accepted the legitimacy of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认可了该合同的合法性。
senses.why: Legitimus in Latin means made in accordance with law, and anything that follows the rules is lawfully made.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 legitimus 意为「依法而立的」，凡是按规则做出的事物都是依法成立的。

senses.title: General acceptance as right and proper
senses.definition: the quality of being accepted as right or proper by the people whom an authority governs
senses.definitionCN: 被掌权者所治理的民众普遍接受为正当的资格
senses.example: A government loses legitimacy when it ignores its citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 一个政府若无视公民，就会失去正当性。
senses.why: Legality can be granted by a court, but legitimacy also needs the acceptance of those who obey, so the sense moves from law to consent.
senses.whyCN: 法律地位可以由法院授予，但正当性还需要被统治者的认同，于是词义由「法律」走向「公意」。

senses.title: Soundness of reasoning or justification
senses.titleCN: 合理性；站得住脚的理由
senses.definition: the quality of being reasonable, defensible, or well justified
senses.definitionCN: 合乎常理、可以辩护或理由充分的品质
senses.example: She doubted the legitimacy of the comparison between the two studies.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀疑把两项研究加以比较是否有根据。
senses.why: The same root says a thing is made according to a rule, and a rule of logic can replace the rule of law, so a well argued claim is legitimate too.
senses.whyCN: 同一词根意为「按规则而成立」，把法律的规则换成逻辑的规则，论证充分的说法也就站得住脚。

senses.title: The legal status of a person born to married parents
senses.definition: the old legal status of a child born within marriage
senses.definitionCN: 旧法律体系中在婚姻内出生的孩子享有的身份
senses.example: In earlier law the legitimacy of a child decided rights of inheritance.
senses.exampleCN: 在早期的法律中，孩子的婚生身份决定继承权。
senses.why: Historically law used the word for children whose birth followed the rules of matrimony, the most concrete legal use of the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 历史上法律用这个词指符合婚配规则出生的孩子，这是同一观念最具体的法律用法。

intro.en: Legitimacy comes from Latin legitimitas, a quality noun formed on legitimus, made according to law, which goes back to lex, law.
intro.cn: legitimacy 来自拉丁语 legitimitas，是由 legitimus（依法而立）构成的性质名词，而 legitimus 上溯到 lex（法律）。

items.en: Lex means law, and legitimus means in accordance with law.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lex 意为法律，legitimus 意为依法的、合法的。

items.en: Legitimitas names the quality of being lawful.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 legitimitas 指合法这一性质。

items.en: French legitime carries the legal sense of lawful birth.
items.cn: 法语 legitime 承接「婚生、合法出生」的法律含义。

items.en: English legitimate names the lawful form before the abstract noun settles in.
items.cn: 英语先固定 legitimate（合法的），随后抽象名词才定形。

items.en: Legitimacy spreads from family law to politics and the lawfulness of powers.
items.cn: 近代英语中 legitimacy 由家庭法扩展到政治，指权力的合法性。

items.en: Twenty century usage adds argument and method, the reasonableness of a claim.
items.cn: 二十世纪之后的用法又加入论证与方法，指主张是否合理。

note.en: Legitimacy sits with legitimate and legitimize on one side of the law, and with legality, validity, and authority on the other.
note.cn: legitimacy 一边与 legitimate、legitimize 同属「依法」词族，另一边与 legality、validity、authority 构成近义义场。

entries.definition: allowed by law or fair and reasonable
entries.definitionCN: 合法的；正当的，是 legitimacy 的形容词形式

entries.definition: to make something lawful or acceptable
entries.definitionCN: 使合法化；使被接受，由同一词根加动词词尾构成

entries.definition: the body that makes laws
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关。与 legitimacy 共享「法律」词根，但词义完全不同

entries.definition: the fact of being allowed by law
entries.definitionCN: 合法性；纯指是否合乎法律条文

entries.definition: the power to give orders and make decisions
entries.definitionCN: 权威；权力，侧重有权发号施令

entries.definition: the state of being based on truth or sound reasoning
entries.definitionCN: 有效性；合理性，侧重论证成立

normalIntro.en: Legitimacy is the noun of legitimate, built on lex, law, so the chain is lex, legal, legitimate, legitimacy.
normalIntro.cn: legitimacy 是 legitimate 的名词形式，词根是 lex（法律），链条为 lex、legal、legitimate、legitimacy。

normal.en: Legitimacy is to legitimate what legality is to legal.
normal.cn: legitimacy 之于 legitimate，正如 legality 之于 legal。

normal.en: Question the legitimacy of is the most common phrase with this noun.
normal.cn: question the legitimacy of 是搭配这个名词最常见的说法。

normal.en: Legitimacy needs both law and public acceptance.
normal.cn: legitimacy 既要有法律依据，也要被公众接受。

normal.en: The prefix il- in illegitimacy turns lawful into unlawful.
normal.cn: 前缀 il- 使 illegitimacy 表示「没有合法性」。

normal.en: Compare legality: legality is about the letter of the law, legitimacy about acceptance.
normal.cn: 对比 legality：前者看法律条文，后者看是否被认可。

abstract.en: Picture a red seal pressed onto a paper and then a room of raised hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚红印压在文件上，随后满屋子的人举起手。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd that stops arguing once someone explains the rules.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在有人讲清规则之后停止争论。

abstract.en: See two columns of figures that finally balance.
abstract.cn: 想象两栏数字最终对上了账。

examples.en: Critics questioned the legitimacy of the new law.
examples.cn: 批评者质疑这项新法律的合法性。

examples.en: The committee gained legitimacy only after a public vote.
examples.cn: 这个委员会在公开投票之后才获得正当性。

examples.en: There is no clear legitimacy to his claim about the causes.
examples.cn: 他关于原因的说法没有站得住脚的合理性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「理基贴么西」——「理」所当然、有基有据，就是「合理性、正当性」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lex（法律）→ legitimus（依法的）→ 晚期拉丁语 legitimitas（合法性）→ 法语 legitime（婚生的；合法的）→ 英语 legitimate → 近代英语 legitimacy（合法性；正当性；合理性），核心义「按规则而立」。

sensesIntro.en: Legitimacy begins with the letter of the law, extends to the consent that keeps an authority accepted, moves to the soundness of an argument, and keeps an old family law sense.
sensesIntro.cn: legitimacy 从法律条文开始，扩展到使权力得以被接受的认同，再到论证的合理性，并保留一个旧有的家庭法义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document that is sealed, voted on, and then filed with the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文件先被盖章，再被投票认可，最后入选归档。

branches.en: The lawful form is the strict legal sense.
branches.cn: 依法成立的形态是最严格的法律义项。

branches.en: Acceptance by those governed is the political sense.
branches.cn: 被治理者接受，这是政治义项。

branches.en: The rule of reasoning is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 讲得通、站得住脚，这是日常义项。

branches.en: Old family law applied the rule of law to a persons birth.
branches.cn: 旧时的家庭法把法律规则用到一个人的出生上。

branches.en: Power needs both the seal and the hands raised in a hall.
branches.cn: 权力既需要那枚印章，也需要大厅里举起的手。

intro.en: Legitimacy is built on the Latin root leg-, law, with the adjective ending -ate and the abstract ending -acy, and the family also has il- and -ize forms.
intro.cn: legitimacy 建立在拉丁语词根 leg-（法律）之上，由形容词词尾 -ate 与抽象名词词尾 -acy 构成，同族还有 il- 与 -ize 形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex means law, legitimus means lawful, and legitimitas names the state of being lawful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lex 意为法律，legitimus 意为依法的，legitimitas 指合法这一状态。

items.example: Lex is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: lex 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Legitimus gives the lawful shape.
items.exampleCN: legitimus 提供「依法」形态。

items.example: Legitimitas is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: legitimitas 是直接前身。

items.example: Legitimate is the adjective behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: legitimate 是这个名词背后的形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示形容词性质的词尾
items.example: The ending -ate forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -acy forms the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -acy 构成抽象名词。

items.example: The verb legitimize adds a verb ending.
items.exampleCN: 动词 legitimize 加上了动词词尾。

items.example: The prefix il- negatives legality too.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 il- 也可用于否定法律相关词。

items.example: Illegitimacy is the negative partner.
items.exampleCN: illegitimacy 是否定的对应词。

items.example: Legal shares the latin root of law.
items.exampleCN: legal 共享拉丁语「法律」词根。

definition_zh: 使合法；使合法化；承认正当；证明正当；规范化
definition_en: to make something lawful or acceptable, or to show that it is fair and reasonable
core_image: 一枚灰色印章落下，盖在文件上，灰色变成法定认可的颜色
scene: 新建的公园没有名分，人们只能偷偷进入；后来市政厅正式承认了它的地位。For years the community garden had no official status, until the city council moved to legitimise it.
sceneCN: 这里 legitimise 是「使合法化、正式承认」（第 2 个义项：使某事物获得法律地位）；句意：这个社区花园多年没有正式身份，直到市议会着手立法承认它。

collocations.zh: 使政府获得合法性认可
使使用武力获得正当性

derivatives.zh: 由 legitim 加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「合法性；正当性」
动词加 -isation，义为「合法化；正当化」
基础形容词，义为「合法的；正当的」
legitimate 加 -ly，义为「合法地；正当地」
加否定前缀 il-，义为「非法的；不正当的」

senses.title: To make something lawful
senses.definition: to make an activity or arrangement lawful or officially permitted
senses.definitionCN: 使某种活动或安排符合法律、获得官方许可
senses.example: The new act legitimises same-sex marriage in the state.
senses.exampleCN: 新的法案使同性婚姻在该州合法。
senses.why: Legitimate comes from Latin legitimus, which means lawful, so the verb means to confer the quality of being lawful.
senses.whyCN: legitimate 源于拉丁语 legitimus（符合法律的），所以这个动词就是「赋予符合法律这一性质」。

senses.title: To give official status
senses.definition: to give an informal or unofficial thing official standing and recognition
senses.definitionCN: 给非正式或未获承认的事物以正式地位和认可
senses.example: The council voted to legitimise the squatters as tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会投票承认这些擅自占住者是合法租户。
senses.why: A thing can be lawful in substance but lack status on paper; the verb then names the act of issuing the stamp.
senses.whyCN: 事物实质上也许并无不妥，只是纸面上缺少名分；这个词便指盖上印章、发出认可的那一步。

senses.title: To justify and defend
senses.definition: to argue or show that something is reasonable and defensible
senses.definitionCN: 论证或表明某事物是合理的、站得住脚的
senses.example: The committee tried to legitimise its decision with new evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会试图用新证据为自己的决定辩护。
senses.why: Justification is the abstract twin of legality: both make a thing stand up under scrutiny.
senses.whyCN: 「正当」是「合法」的抽象孪生兄弟：两者都让事情在被审视时站得住脚。

senses.title: To make accepted by people
senses.definition: to make something perceived as normal, proper, or acceptable in society
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物在社会中被视为正常、正当或可以接受
senses.example: Popular films helped legitimise the new slang among teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 流行电影帮助这种新俚语在青少年中获得认可。
senses.why: Law is only one maker of legitimacy; everyday approval by a community does the same work socially.
senses.whyCN: 法律只是「正当性」的来源之一；社群日常的认可在社会层面做的是同一件事。

senses.title: To make it right to record
senses.definition: to make an entry, practice, or procedure acceptable under the rules of a system such as accounting
senses.definitionCN: 使某项记录、做法或程序符合某一体系（如会计）的规则
senses.example: The auditor refused to legitimise the irregular payment.
senses.exampleCN: 审计员拒绝把那笔不合规的付款做合法处理。
senses.why: Accounting applies the Latin lawful sense to numbers: an entry is legitimised when it fits the books.
senses.whyCN: 会计把拉丁语「合乎规矩」这一层含义用在数字上：一条记录合乎账面规则，就算被合法化。

senses.title: To pass a law about it
senses.definition: to bring something under statutory law by legislation or formal regulation
senses.definitionCN: 通过立法或正式规章把某事物纳入法律规定
senses.example: Parliament finally legitimised the traditional grazing rights.
senses.exampleCN: 议会终于立法承认了那些传统的放牧权。
senses.why: This is sense 01 carried out by the legal machine itself: a statute makes the thing lawful.
senses.whyCN: 这是第一个义项由立法机器亲自执行：成文法让该事物变得合乎法律。

senses.title: To frame as legitimate
senses.titleCN: 给某说法贴上正当标签
senses.definition: to describe a claim, action, or label in a way that makes it seem acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 用某种说法描述主张、行动或标签，使其显得可以接受
senses.example: Calling the invasion a rescue mission legitimises it.
senses.exampleCN: 把入侵称作救援行动，就是在给它正名。
senses.why: Language is a stamp too: a flattering frame can legitimise what a plain description would not.
senses.whyCN: 语言也是一枚印章：一个好看的框架能给平实说法无法辩护的事盖上认可。

senses.title: To formalise by usage
senses.definition: to make a convention official by repeatedly using or following it
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复使用或遵循，使某一惯例获得正式地位
senses.example: A single court ruling legitimised the informal practice.
senses.exampleCN: 一份判决就让这种非正式做法获得了正式地位。
senses.why: What people do again and again becomes the norm, and the norm eventually receives the official mark.
senses.whyCN: 人们反复做的事变成惯例，惯例最终被盖上正式的印章。
