latinIntro.en: Latin lex, law, yields legitimus, lawful, and legitimare, to make lawful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lex（法律）派生出 legitimus（合乎法律的）与 legitimare（使合法）。

items.example: The root leg carries the idea of law here.
items.exampleCN: 词根 leg 在这里承载「法律」的意思。

items.example: Legitimate is the base adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: legitimate 是这个词族的基底形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ize is the standard American form.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 是标准的美国拼写形式。

items.example: Legitimize is the American verb form.
items.exampleCN: legitimize 是美式动词形式。

items.example: Legitimise is the British spelling.
items.exampleCN: legitimise 是英式拼写。

items.example: The suffix -ization forms legitimization.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ization 构成 legitimization。

items.example: Legitimacy names the quality the verb gives.
items.exampleCN: legitimacy 指这个动词所赋予的性质。

items.example: The prefix il- makes illegitimate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 il- 构成 illegitimate。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms legitimately.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 legitimately。

definition_zh: 有闲的；悠闲的；从容不迫的；属于有闲阶层的
definition_en: having plenty of free time, or marked by unhurried ease and comfort
core_image: 一个人坐在藤椅上慢慢翻书，旁边的茶还冒着热气，没有闹钟
scene: 阳台上，老人不赶时间，只是翻着旧相册喝茶，楼下的人都在匆匆赶路。The old man on the balcony was clearly a leisured man, with nowhere to hurry to.
sceneCN: 这里 leisured 是「有闲的、不匆忙的」（第 1 个义项：拥有大量闲暇时间）；句意：阳台上的老人一看就是位有闲人，没有任何地方要赶。

pos.zh: 从容不迫的；属于有闲阶层的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「闲暇；空闲时间」
加 -ly 构成，义为「悠闲的；不慌不忙的」，也可作副词
leisurely 加 -ness，义为「从容不迫的状态」

senses.title: Having plenty of free time
senses.definition: having a lot of free time, especially because work is not a necessity
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量闲暇时间，尤指不必为生计劳作
senses.example: The village attracted wealthy, leisured visitors each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 每年夏天，这座村庄都吸引来有钱又有闲的访客。
senses.why: Leisured is leisure turned into an adjective by the suffix -ed, so it describes anyone who possesses free time.
senses.whyCN: leisured 是 leisure 加后缀 -ed 变成的形容词，用来描述拥有自由时间的人。

senses.title: Unhurried and gentle in pace
senses.definition: marked by an unhurried, easeful pace or manner
senses.definitionCN: 以不慌不忙、放松的节奏或姿态为特征
senses.example: He spoke in a leisured drawl that made deadlines seem absurd.
senses.exampleCN: 他用慢悠悠的拖腔说话，让截止日期显得荒唐可笑。
senses.why: If someone has time to spare, their movements and speech lose the hurry, so the adjective drifts from owning time to showing ease.
senses.whyCN: 人有富余的时间，动作和言语自然就不急，于是这个词从「拥有时间」滑向「显出从容」。

senses.title: Belonging to the leisured class
senses.definition: characteristic of a social group that lives on income rather than daily labour
senses.definitionCN: 具有靠收入而非日常劳动生活的那一社会群体的特征
senses.example: The novel mocks the leisured tastes of the upper class.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说嘲讽了上层阶级那种有闲的品味。
senses.why: Economists and sociologists fixed the word to a class, so leisured became a label for a whole lifestyle of inherited income.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家和社会学家把这个词固定到一个阶层上，leisured 于是成了靠继承收入过活的一整套生活方式的标签。

senses.title: Comfortable rather than rushed
senses.definition: describing a setting or period that feels comfortable, relaxed, and free of pressure
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种舒适、放松、没有压力的环境或时光
senses.example: They spent a leisured afternoon in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在花园里度过了一个安逸的下午。
senses.why: The adjective spread from people to places and hours, so any comfortable stretch of time can be called leisured.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从人扩展到场所与时光，任何舒适宽裕的一段时间都可以称作 leisured。

senses.title: Deliberate and careful
senses.definition: done slowly and carefully, with enough time for quality rather than speed
senses.definitionCN: 不慌不忙地细做，有足够时间顾及质量而非速度
senses.example: The book offers a leisured reading of every poem.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对每一首诗都做了从容细致的解读。
senses.why: Time in hand allows detail, so what is done at leisure gets done with care, and the adjective carries that care.
senses.whyCN: 手头有时间才顾得上细节，闲下来做的事往往更细致，这个形容词便带上了这层用心。

senses.title: Activities that fill free time
senses.definition: used for activities that people do to fill free time, often viewed as light or decorative
senses.definitionCN: 指人们用来填满空闲时间的活动，常被视为轻松或装饰性的
senses.example: His leisured pursuits were chess, fishing, and long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 他用来消磨闲暇的爱好是下棋、钓鱼和长途散步。
senses.why: If a person is leisured, their hobbies are too, so the word came to modify the activities that fill spare hours.
senses.whyCN: 人既然有闲，他的爱好也就有闲，于是这个词开始修饰填满空余时间的活动。

senses.title: Not bound by working hours
senses.definition: free from the fixed schedule of paid work, whether through wealth or retirement
senses.definitionCN: 不受固定上班时间约束，或因富有、或因退休而自由
senses.example: Retirees form a large, leisured group of readers.
senses.exampleCN: 退休者构成了一大群有闲的读者。
senses.why: The word is about the absence of clock time, so anyone outside the working day, whatever the reason, fits it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词说的是不受钟表支配，所以任何处在工作日之外的人，不论原因如何，都能用上它。

senses.title: Rich enough not to work
senses.definition: describing the condition of having enough income to live without working
senses.definitionCN: 形容收入足够、无需工作便可生活的一种状况
senses.example: The portrait shows a leisured and rather bored young man.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像画的是一个富有闲散、有些无聊的年轻人。
senses.why: Historically leisure and wealth travelled together, so the adjective often implies money behind the free time.
senses.whyCN: 历史上闲暇与财富总是结伴而行，所以这个形容词常常暗含自由时间背后的钱。

intro.en: Leisured is formed from leisure with the suffix -ed, and leisure descends from Old French leisir, related to Latin licere, to be allowed.
intro.cn: leisured 由 leisure 加后缀 -ed 构成，而 leisure 来自古法语 leisir，与拉丁语 licere（被允许）相关。

items.en: Licere means to be allowed or permitted.
items.cn: licere 意为被允许、获准。

items.en: Licentia names freedom or permission, the abstract form of the verb.
items.cn: licentia 表示自由或许可，是动词的抽象名词形式。

items.en: Leisir, influenced by loisir, means to be permitted and also names free time.
items.cn: leisir 受 loisir 影响，既有「获准」之意，也指自由时间。

items.en: Leisure enters English as the name of time free from duty.
items.cn: leisure 进入英语，指不受职责占用的时间。

items.en: The adjective leisured grows from the noun to describe people with free time.
items.cn: 形容词 leisured 由名词生长出来，形容有自由时间的人。

items.en: Economists fix the phrase leisured class, and the adjective covers ease in general.
items.cn: 经济学家固定下「有闲阶层」的说法，这个形容词也开始泛指从容闲适。

note.en: Leisured stands beside the leisure word family and also beside adjectives for relaxed and idle ways of living.
note.cn: leisured 身边既有 leisure 词族，也有表示悠闲、闲散生活的形容词。

entries.definition: time free from work or duties
entries.definitionCN: 不受工作或职责占用的时间

entries.definition: relaxed and unhurried
entries.definitionCN: 悠闲的；不慌不忙的

entries.definition: comfortable clothing for free time
entries.definitionCN: 休闲装

entries.definition: calm and free from tension
entries.definitionCN: 放松的；轻松的

entries.definition: not working or not busy
entries.definitionCN: 闲着的；不忙的

entries.definition: not fast or rushed
entries.definitionCN: 从容的；不匆忙的

normalIntro.en: Leisured adds -ed to leisure, so it describes people and times that are full of free hours.
normalIntro.cn: leisured 是在 leisure 后加 -ed，用来描述充满自由时间的人或时光。

normal.en: The noun is leisure, and the phrase at leisure means with free time to spare.
normal.cn: 名词是 leisure，常与时间搭配，如有一点闲暇。

normal.en: The adjective leisurely describes how something is done; leisured describes who has the time.
normal.cn: leisurely 描述做事的方式，leisured 描述谁拥有时间。

normal.en: The suffix -ed on a noun means having or possessing, as in leisured and bearded.
normal.cn: 名词后缀 -ed 表示拥有某种特征，如 leisured 与 bearded。

normal.en: The set phrase leisured class names people who live without daily labour.
normal.cn: 固定说法 leisured class 指不靠日常劳作生活的人。

normal.en: Latin licere, to be allowed, links leisure with freedom to choose what to do.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 licere（被允许）把闲暇与「自由选择做什么」连在一起。

abstract.en: See a man in a rattan chair with a cup of tea and no clock on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人坐在藤椅上喝茶，墙上没有钟。

abstract.en: Picture a street where everyone walks slow and nothing beeps.
abstract.cn: 想象一条人人慢走、没有提示音催促的街道。

abstract.en: Imagine a velvet portrait of a rich man with nothing on his schedule.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅丝绒油画，画着一位日程空空的富人。

examples.en: The novel is set among the leisured families of the countryside.
examples.cn: 这部小说以乡村那些有闲人家为背景。

examples.en: At a leisured pace, the village rebuilt its old market square.
examples.cn: 村子以从容的节奏重建了旧日的集市广场。

examples.en: Leisured afternoons made her a careful reader rather than a fast one.
examples.cn: 悠闲的午后让她成为仔细的读者，而不是快速的读者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累着」的反面——忙得累着了才想闲下来，于是 leisured 记成「不累、有闲」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 licere（被允许）→ licentia（许可；自由）→ 古法语 leisir、loisir（获准；自由时间）→ 英语 leisure（闲暇）→ 形容词 leisured（有闲的）。核心义「获准自由支配的时间」。

sensesIntro.en: Leisured starts as a class adjective meaning having free time, then moves to unhurried manner, comfortable settings, careful work, and finally leisure activities.
sensesIntro.cn: leisured 先作描述阶层的形容词，表示「拥有闲暇」，再转向从容的举止、安逸的环境、细致的工夫，最后指消磨闲暇的活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person in a rattan chair with tea and no clock in sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：藤椅上喝茶的人，墙上没有钟。

branches.en: Having free time is the core adjectival sense.
branches.cn: 拥有闲暇是这个形容词的核心义项。

branches.en: Unhurried pace and careful work both come from having time in hand.
branches.cn: 从容的节奏与细致的工夫都来自手头有时间。

branches.en: The class label and the implication of wealth point to the same social fact.
branches.cn: 阶层标签与暗含的富有指向同一个社会事实。

branches.en: Comfort and pursuits both transfer the quality from people to things.
branches.cn: 安逸与消遣都把这种特质从人转移到事物上。

branches.en: Freedom from rota and wealth without needful labour are two routes to the same leisure.
branches.cn: 不受排班约束与富有而无需劳作，是通向同一种闲暇的两条路。

intro.en: Leisured is the noun leisure with the adjective suffix -ed, inside a small family of leisure words.
intro.cn: leisured 是名词 leisure 加形容词后缀 -ed，属于一个规模不大的 leisure 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin licere means to be allowed, and licentia names freedom, the source of the French word for free time.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 licere 意为被允许，licentia 表示自由，这是法语中「自由时间」一词的来源。

items.meaning: to be allowed, to be permitted
items.example: The root lic shows the idea of permission.
items.exampleCN: 词根 lic 体现「许可」之意。

items.example: Leisure is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: leisure 是这个词族的基底名词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms leisured from leisure.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 把 leisure 变成 leisured。

items.example: Leisured describes people with plenty of free time.
items.exampleCN: leisured 描述拥有大量闲暇的人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the manner adjective leisurely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成表示方式的形容词 leisurely。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms leisureliness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 leisureliness。

items.example: Leisurewear joins leisure and wear.
items.exampleCN: leisurewear 由 leisure 与 wear 组合而成。

items.example: The phrase at leisure keeps the free time sense.
items.exampleCN: 短语 at leisure 保留「闲暇」的含义。

items.example: Leisured class is the fixed phrase for rich non-workers.
items.exampleCN: leisured class 是富而不劳者的固定说法。

definition_zh: 柠檬水；柠檬汽水；柠檬饮料
definition_en: a sweet drink made from lemon juice, water, and sugar, or a fizzy drink with lemon flavor
core_image: 玻璃杯里浮着柠檬片，冰块在淡黄色液体中碰出清脆的响声
scene: 午后的院子里阳光很毒，孩子捧着一杯冰凉的黄色饮料，冰块叮当作响。The children sold lemonade from a little stand at the end of the road.
sceneCN: 这里 lemonade 是「柠檬水」（第 1 个义项：柠檬汁、糖和凉水调成的酸甜饮料）；句意为孩子们在路口的小摊上卖柠檬水。画面可辨识：玻璃柠檬摊、手写招牌、一罐冰块、切开的柠檬。

pos.zh: 柠檬水；柠檬汽水；柠檬饮料

derivatives.zh: 柠檬；由同一个法语词根 limon 来的基础词，lemonade 就是它加上 -ade 做成的饮料
由 lemonade 加 maker 构成的复合词，义为「柠檬水制作者」，属于常见的复合构词，词典少见
口语中加 -y 构成的形容词，义为「带柠檬水味的、淡黄色的」，使用范围较窄

senses.title: A sweet and sour drink made from lemons
senses.titleCN: 柠檬水（柠檬汁加糖水调成）
senses.definition: a drink made by mixing lemon juice with water and sugar
senses.definitionCN: 把柠檬汁与水和糖调和做成的饮料
senses.example: She squeezed two lemons and made a pitcher of lemonade.
senses.exampleCN: 她挤了两个柠檬，做了一大壶柠檬水。
senses.why: The French suffix -ade marks a fruit drink, so the very ending of the word announces a beverage rather than a fruit.
senses.whyCN: 法语后缀 -ade 表示「水果做成的饮料」，所以词尾本身就宣告这是一款饮品，而不是果子。

senses.title: A sweet fizzy drink with lemon flavor
senses.definition: a commercially made carbonated soft drink flavored with lemon, often cloudy and sweet
senses.definitionCN: 工厂生产的、带柠檬味的含气软饮料，常常是浑浊甜口的柠檬汽水
senses.example: He poured cloudy lemonade over ice for the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他给客人们倒上加了冰的浑浊柠檬汽水。
senses.why: Once factories began bottling the drink, the same name covered the sparkling version sold in shops.
senses.whyCN: 当工厂开始灌装这种饮料后，同一个名字就顺带覆盖了商店里出售的含气版本。

senses.title: A homemade drink sold from a small stall
senses.definition: a home-made drink often sold by children from a small roadside table
senses.definitionCN: 儿童在路边小桌上出售的自制柠檬饮料
senses.example: She set up a lemonade stand to raise money for the animal shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 她摆了一个柠檬水小摊，为动物收容所筹钱。
senses.why: The drink became a small social ritual, and the stall image grew out of the pitcher and the paper cups.
senses.whyCN: 这杯饮料成了一种小型社交仪式，小摊的意象正是从水壶和纸杯这类日常画面里长出来的。

senses.title: A drink that is mostly water and sugar
senses.definition: a light drink that is mostly water, sugar, and only a little lemon juice
senses.definitionCN: 以水、糖为主，只加少量柠檬汁的清淡饮料
senses.example: The lemonade at the party was so watery that nobody wanted a second glass.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会上那杯柠檬水太淡了，没有人想要第二杯。
senses.why: Because the recipe balances juice against a large amount of water, the same word can describe a slightly diluted result.
senses.whyCN: 由于配方是用大量水去平衡果汁，所以同一个词也能形容略被稀释的成品。

intro.en: Lemonade joins lemon, borrowed through Old French from Arabic, with the French drink suffix -ade.
intro.cn: lemonade 由 lemon（经古法语借自阿拉伯语）与法语饮料后缀 -ade 组合而成。

items.en: The fruit name is usually traced to Arabic laymun, which spread with cultivated citrus through the Mediterranean.
items.cn: 一般认为果名可追溯到阿拉伯语 laymun，随栽培柑橘传到地中海各地。

items.en: Old French limon names the citrus fruit and passes it into English.
items.cn: 古法语 limon 指柑橘类果实，并把它传入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ade marks a drink made from a fruit, a pattern shared by orangeade and others, giving limonade.
items.cn: 法语后缀 -ade 表示「某水果做成的饮料」，与 orangeade 等同构，形成 limonade。

items.en: The borrowed drink name is reshaped to echo English lemon.
items.cn: 借入的饮料名被改写成与英语 lemon 呼应的形式。

items.en: The word covers bottled fizzy drinks as well as home-made ones.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义扩展到瓶装汽水，也保留自制柠檬水的含义。

note.en: Lemonade sits in a small family of fruit drinks, and also resembles the plain fruit name lemon.
note.cn: lemonade 属于「水果饮料」这一小类词，外形又与单纯的水果名 lemon 极为接近。

entries.definition: the yellow citrus fruit
entries.definitionCN: 柠檬这种黄色柑橘果实，是 lemonade 去掉饮料后缀后的基础词

entries.definition: a sweet drink made from oranges
entries.definitionCN: 橙汁饮料，共用同一个饮料后缀 -ade

entries.definition: a drink made from limes
entries.definitionCN: 青柠饮料，同样是「水果加 -ade」的构词模式

entries.definition: a sweet fizzy soft drink
entries.definitionCN: 甜味的含气软饮料，在美式英语里可泛指柠檬汽水一类

entries.definition: a sweet fruit syrup drunk when mixed with water
entries.definitionCN: 英国英语中指兑水喝的甜水果糖浆，做法与家庭柠檬水相近

entries.definition: a concentrated fruit drink to be mixed with water
entries.definitionCN: 英国英语中指需兑水稀释的水果饮品浓缩汁

normalIntro.en: Lemonade is lemon plus a drink suffix: the fruit name tells you what it is made of, and the ending tells you it is something to drink.
normalIntro.cn: lemonade 就是 lemon 加上饮料后缀：前面的水果名告诉你原料，后面的词尾告诉你这是喝的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -ade marks drinks made from fruit, as in orangeade and limeade.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ade 标记「水果做成的饮料」，orangeade 与 limeade 都遵循这个模式。

normal.en: Lemonade is lemonade because lemon is its fruit.
normal.cn: lemonade 之所以叫这个名字，是因为 lemon 就是它的原料水果。

normal.en: A glass of lemonade is lemon juice, water, and sugar in a glass.
normal.cn: a glass of lemonade 就是一杯柠檬汁、水和糖调成的饮料。

normal.en: A lemonade stand is a common picture of childhood selling.
normal.cn: lemonade stand 是儿童摆摊卖饮料的经典画面。

normal.en: When life gives you lemons, make lemonade: the proverb turns sour fruit into a sweet drink.
normal.cn: 谚语里说「生活给你柠檬，就做柠檬水」：把酸果子变成甜饮料。

abstract.en: Picture a jug of pale yellow drink clouded by lemon pulp.
abstract.cn: 想象一壶淡黄色饮料，里面因柠檬果肉而呈浑浊状。

abstract.en: Hear the fizz of carbonated lemonade rising through ice cubes.
abstract.cn: 想象汽水里的小气泡在冰块间不断上升。

abstract.en: See a child at a small table with a hand-painted sign and paper cups.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子守着小桌子，桌上手写招牌和一摞纸杯。

examples.en: On hot days we keep a jug of lemonade in the fridge.
examples.cn: 天热时我们会在冰箱里放一壶柠檬水。

examples.en: Two neighbours set up a lemonade stand for the school fair.
examples.cn: 两位邻居为学校义卖摆了一个柠檬水小摊。

examples.en: The fizzy lemonade hissed as she opened the bottle.
examples.cn: 她拧开瓶盖时，含气柠檬水发出嘶嘶声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乐么…内德」——夏天喝一杯加冰的柠檬水，人就会「乐么」起来，咧嘴一笑；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 limonade 由 limon「柠檬」+ -ade「（水果）饮料后缀」构成；limon 与英语 lemon 同源，一般认为源自阿拉伯语 laymun，随柑橘栽培传入地中海。词源本身没有存疑部分，只有传入英语的拼写年代细节偶有出入。

sensesIntro.en: Lemonade starts as the sour-sweet drink mixed at home, spreads to carbonated bottled versions, then names the small roadside stall, and finally the watery result of a careless recipe.
sensesIntro.cn: lemonade 先指家里现调的酸甜饮料，再扩展到瓶装含气版本，随后指路边小摊这一场景，最后还能形容配方随意、口味很淡的成品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass of pale yellow drink with ice cubes and a lemon slice on the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯淡黄色饮料，冰块浮动，杯沿挂着一片柠檬。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN: lemon juice, water and sugar combine into the everyday drink.
branches.cn: 厨房线：柠檬汁、水和糖调成最日常的那一杯。

branches.en: THE SHOP SHELF: bottling and carbonation move the same name into fizzy soft drinks.
branches.cn: 货架线：灌装与充气让同一个名字进入含气软饮料。

branches.en: THE STREET: children selling cups turn the drink into a social scene.
branches.cn: 街角线：孩子卖杯装饮料，把它变成一则社交场景。

branches.en: THE WEAK RECIPE: too much water and too little juice produce the faint version.
branches.cn: 寡淡线：水多汁少，就出现了口味很淡的版本。

branches.en: Home-made, bottled and stall-sold lemonade all share the same sour-sweet recipe.
branches.cn: 自制、瓶装和摊售的柠檬水共享同一套酸甜配方。

intro.en: Lemonade is built from the fruit noun lemon and the French drink suffix -ade, a pattern repeated in limeade and orangeade.
intro.cn: lemonade 由水果名词 lemon 与法语饮料后缀 -ade 构成，limeade 与 orangeade 都沿用这一模式。

latinIntro.en: The suffix descends from Latin -ata, a past-participle ending that French turned into a noun tail for drinks and products.
latinIntro.cn: 这个后缀可追溯到拉丁语 -ata（过去分词词尾），法语把它发展成标记饮料与制品的名词词尾。

items.example: Lemon names the fruit that gives the drink its flavor.
items.exampleCN: lemon 指为饮料提供风味的果实。

items.meaning: a drink made from the named fruit
items.example: The suffix -ade forms lemonade and orangeade.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ade 构成 lemonade 与 orangeade。

items.example: Lemonade keeps the full drink sense.
items.exampleCN: lemonade 保留完整的饮料含义。

items.example: Limeade follows the same suffix pattern.
items.exampleCN: limeade 遵循同样的后缀模式。

items.example: Orangeade shows the fruit-plus-ade mold.
items.exampleCN: orangeade 展示了「水果加 -ade」的构词模具。

items.meaning: several servings or types of the drink
items.example: The plural counts servings or kinds.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式用来计杯数或种类。

items.meaning: an informal name for pink lemonade
items.meaningCN: 粉红柠檬水的口语简称，属于构词活跃的例子，非正式用法
items.example: The casual shortening shows how product names grow new words.
items.exampleCN: 这种口语缩略显示出商品名如何催生新词。

items.meaning: having the quality of the base
items.example: The suffix -y forms lemonadey in casual speech.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 在口语中构成 lemonadey。

items.example: Old French limon carries the fruit into the drink name.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 limon 把果实名带进了饮料词。

latinEntries.meaning: past participle ending, later a product noun tail
latinEntries.meaningCN: 过去分词词尾，后转为表示制品的名词词尾

definition_zh: 宽容的；宽大的；宽厚的；处罚从轻的
definition_en: not strict or severe in punishing or in setting rules, and willing to let small faults pass
core_image: 老师把举起的尺子轻轻放下，让它贴着桌面，而不是落在学生的手心里
scene: 试卷交晚了，孩子低着头站在办公室里等批评，老师却先问原因，然后只轻轻提醒了一句。The judge was lenient with the young driver who had only just passed his test.
sceneCN: 这里 lenient 是「宽大的、处罚从轻的」（第 2 个义项：在惩罚或执法时从轻处理）；句意为法官对刚刚通过驾驶考试的年轻司机从轻处理。画面可辨识：法庭木槌、驾驶执照、放下的软垫。

derivatives.zh: 宽容、从宽处理；由形容词加 -cy 构成，把「宽」变成一项态度或措施
宽容；与 leniency 同义，词尾略异，书面语中更少见
缓和地；由同源的 lenitive（缓和的、缓和剂）构成的副词，药学语境常见

senses.title: Not strict in dealing with faults
senses.titleCN: 宽容的：对小过错不苛责
senses.definition: not severe in judging people, and willing to forgive small faults instead of punishing them
senses.definitionCN: 对人评判不严厉，愿意原谅小过错而不去惩罚
senses.example: She is lenient with students who are late for the first lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 她对第一节迟到的学生很宽容。
senses.why: Latin lenire means to soften or soothe, so a lenient person softens the edge of judgement that would otherwise cut.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lenire 意为「使变软、抚慰」，所以宽容的人把原本会划伤人的评判之刃磨软了。

senses.title: Light in punishment or enforcement
senses.definition: giving a punishment or applying a law less severely than is usual or allowed
senses.definitionCN: 施行的处罚或执法比通常或允许的更轻
senses.example: The court gave him a lenient sentence because he had confessed at once.
senses.exampleCN: 因为他立刻认罪，法院给了他一个从轻的判决。
senses.why: From a soft manner of judging, the word narrowed to the measurable lightness of a penalty itself.
senses.whyCN: 从评判方式「软」出发，词义收窄到处罚本身可衡量的「轻」上。

senses.title: Relaxed in rules and standards
senses.definition: having rules or standards that are not strict or demanding
senses.definitionCN: 规定或标准不严格、要求不高
senses.example: The school has lenient rules about hair colour and jewellery.
senses.exampleCN: 学校对发色和首饰的规定很宽松。
senses.why: The same softness applied to rules rather than people gives the set-up side of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 把这种「软」用到规则而不是人身上，就得到词义中「规定设置宽松」的那一面。

senses.title: Mild in treating a condition
senses.definition: mild in effect, used for a treatment that soothes rather than irritates
senses.definitionCN: 作用温和、以舒缓为主而不刺激的（多指疗法）
senses.example: Doctors suggest a lenient diet of soft food while the ulcer heals.
senses.exampleCN: 溃疡愈合期间，医生建议采用以软食为主的温和饮食。
senses.why: The oldest sense of lenire was to soothe a body, and medicine keeps that bodily softness alive.
senses.whyCN: lenire 最古老的含义就是抚慰身体，医学语境把这个与身体相关的「软」保留了下来。

intro.en: Lenient comes from Latin lenis, soft or mild, through the verb lenire, to soften.
intro.cn: lenient 来自拉丁语 lenis（柔软的、温和的），经由动词 lenire（使变软）而来。

items.en: The root is usually reconstructed as a form meaning soft or gentle, though the exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为词根是表示「柔软、温和」的形式，但确切重构形态存疑。

items.en: Lenis means soft, mild, or gentle, and the verb lenire means to soften or soothe.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lenis 意为柔软、温和，动词 lenire 意为使变软、抚慰。

items.en: During the revival of classical Latin, the verb lenire uses its participle leniens, soft-making.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语复兴时期，动词 lenire 的现在分词 leniens 表示「使变软的」。

items.en: Lenient first appears with the sense of soothing or softening in medical or general prose.
items.cn: lenient 最早出现在医学或一般散文中，意思是「有舒缓作用的」。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word had narrowed to mildness in judgement, punishment, and rules.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，词义收窄为在评判、处罚和规则上的宽容。

note.en: Lenient shares its root with leniency, lenis, and lenitive, and stands close to milder words such as tolerant and easy-going.
note.cn: lenient 与 leniency、lenis、lenitive 同根，语义上靠近 tolerant、easy-going 这类表示「不严厉」的词。

entries.definition: the quality of being lenient
entries.definitionCN: 宽容、从宽处理，是 lenient 的派生名词

entries.definition: mercy or mildness
entries.definitionCN: 宽恕、温和，与 leniency 同义的变体

entries.definition: a soft consonant sound in phonetics
entries.definitionCN: 语音学中的「软辅音」，保留拉丁语 lenis「柔软」的本义

entries.definition: accepting beliefs or behaviour one does not share
entries.definitionCN: 容忍与自己不同的信仰或行为，偏「接受差异」

entries.definition: relaxed and not easily upset
entries.definitionCN: 随和的、不较真的，口语中形容人的性格

entries.definition: demanding that rules be obeyed exactly
entries.definitionCN: 严格的，是 lenient 的反义对照

normalIntro.en: Lenient keeps the Latin idea of softness: what is lenient has been softened, whether it is a judge, a rule, or a cure.
normalIntro.cn: lenient 保留了拉丁语「柔软」的内核：无论是法官、规则还是疗法，凡 lenient 之处都被「软化」了。

normal.en: The root leni- means soft, as in lenis and lenitive.
normal.cn: 词根 leni- 表示「柔软」，lenis 与 lenitive 都带着这层意思。

normal.en: The noun is leniency, as in ask for leniency in court.
normal.cn: 名词是 leniency，法庭上「请求从宽处理」就是 ask for leniency。

normal.en: A lenient sentence sends you home with a fine instead of a cell.
normal.cn: a lenient sentence 就是判个罚金就让你回家，而不是关进牢房。

normal.en: Be lenient with beginners, but never lenient with facts.
normal.cn: 对初学者可以宽容，但对事实永远不能宽容。

normal.en: Compare strict: strict presses, lenient lets go.
normal.cn: 对比 strict：strict 是紧压，lenient 是松手。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid flat on a desk instead of raised in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子平躺在桌面上，而不是高高举起。

abstract.en: Think of a thick cushion under a judgement, taking the shock out of it.
abstract.cn: 想象判决下面垫了一块厚垫子，把冲击力吸走了。

abstract.en: See a gate with a wide gap, so that people walk through without squeezing.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门留了很宽的口子，人们走进去不必挤。

examples.en: Some parents feel the school is too lenient about mobile phones.
examples.cn: 有些家长觉得学校对手机的管理太宽松了。

examples.en: He was given a lenient sentence after he repaid the money.
examples.cn: 他归还钱款后获得了从轻判决。

examples.en: The coach is lenient with beginners but firm with senior players.
examples.cn: 教练对初学者很宽容，对老队员却要求严格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「理你恩」——法官对犯人说：我还「理会」你的「恩」情，所以从轻发落；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lenis「柔软的、温和的」→ 动词 lenire「使变软、抚慰」→ 现在分词 leniens → 十七世纪英语 lenient「有舒缓作用的」，后引申为「放宽评判与处罚」；更早的印欧语词根重构形式存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Lenient begins as the softness of a soothing hand, then extends to the softness of a judge, a penalty, a rule, and finally a gentle treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: lenient 起初是抚慰之手的那种「软」，随后扩展到法官的态度、处罚的轻重、规则的宽严，最后回到医学里温和的疗法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand opens and lowers, and the blow that was coming never lands.
core.cn: 核心意象：举起的手张开又放下，本来要落下的那一击始终没有落下。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a lenient judge or teacher softens judgement and lets small faults pass.
branches.cn: 人物线：宽容的法官或老师把评判放软，让小错过去。

branches.en: THE PENALTY: softness applied to a sentence makes the punishment measurably lighter.
branches.cn: 处罚线：把「软」用在判决上，惩罚就变得明显更轻。

branches.en: THE RULE: softness applied to standards makes the rules loose rather than demanding.
branches.cn: 规则线：把「软」用在标准上，规定就变得宽松而不苛刻。

branches.en: THE BODY: the oldest idea of softening returns in gentle medical treatments.
branches.cn: 身体线：最古老的「使变软」在温和疗法中回归。

branches.en: A lenient manner and a lenient sentence both spare someone the full edge of a judgement.
branches.cn: 宽容的态度与从轻的判决，都在替某人挡掉评判的锋芒。

intro.en: Lenient is built on the Latin root len-, soft, which also yields lenitive, leniency, and the phonetic term lenis.
intro.cn: lenient 建立在拉丁词根 len-（柔软）之上，lenitive、leniency 以及语音学术语 lenis 都出自同一个词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin lenis means soft, and lenire means to soften; the participle leniens supplies the shape of lenient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lenis 意为柔软，lenire 意为使变软；分词 leniens 提供了 lenient 的形式。

items.example: Lenis supplies the core soft image.
items.exampleCN: lenis 提供「柔软」的核心意象。

items.example: Lenire turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: lenire 把形容词变成动作。

items.meaningCN: 表示正在做某事或带有某性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ent builds lenient from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 把动词词干构成 lenient。

items.example: Lenient moves from soothing to forgiving.
items.exampleCN: lenient 从「舒缓」过渡到「宽恕」。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -cy forms leniency.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cy 构成 leniency。

items.example: Leniency is what a lawyer asks for.
items.exampleCN: leniency 是律师常为本方争取的东西。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms leniently.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 leniently。

items.example: Lenitive keeps the medical side of the root.
items.exampleCN: lenitive 保留了词根的医学一面。

items.meaningCN: 软辅音，即发音较柔和的辅音
items.example: The technical phrase echoes the Latin sense of soft.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语回响着拉丁语「软」的含义。

definition_zh: 豹；花豹；豹皮
definition_en: a large wild cat with a yellowish coat covered in dark rosette spots, found in Africa and Asia
core_image: 一只金黄色的大猫伏在树枝上，身上落满黑边梅花斑，长尾垂下来轻轻摆动
scene: 国家公园的灌木丛里，巡护员低声示意大家别出声。A leopard rested on a low branch, its spotted coat almost invisible in the dappled light.
sceneCN: 这里 leopard 是「花豹」（第 1 个义项：金黄色毛皮、带黑色梅花斑的大型野生猫科动物）；句意为一只花豹趴在低矮的树枝上，斑纹毛皮在斑驳光影里几乎看不见。画面可辨识：粗壮树杈、垂下的长尾、白色胡须。

derivatives.zh: 母豹；由 leopard 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，把性别单独标出
雪豹；由 snow 与 leopard 组成的复合词，指中亚高寒山地的近亲猫科动物
豹的；似豹的；由 leopard 加拉丁形容词词尾 -ine 构成，专业文献少见

senses.title: The spotted wild cat
senses.titleCN: 花豹：带梅花斑的大型野猫
senses.definition: a large wild cat of Africa and Asia with a pale yellow coat marked by dark rosettes
senses.definitionCN: 分布于非洲和亚洲、淡黄色毛皮上带深色梅花斑的大型野猫
senses.example: A leopard can drag a kill heavier than itself up a tree.
senses.exampleCN: 花豹能把比自己更重的猎物拖上树。
senses.why: The Greek name combines the lion and the pard, so the very word pairs two fierce cats with one spotted body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语名字把「狮」与「豹」并在一起，所以这个词本身就是两张猛兽面孔合成一身斑点。

senses.title: A spotted pattern named after the cat
senses.titleCN: 豹纹：以豹命名的大斑点花纹
senses.definition: a print of irregular dark spots on a golden ground, used in clothing and design
senses.definitionCN: 金色底上散布不规则深色大斑点的花纹，用于服装与设计
senses.example: She wore a coat in leopard print with black leather boots.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿一件豹纹大衣，配黑色皮靴。
senses.why: Once the animal name became familiar, its coat pattern could stand alone as a design noun.
senses.whyCN: 当动物名变得耳熟之后，它的毛皮花纹就能单独当设计名词来用。

senses.title: The skin or fur used as material
senses.definition: the skin or spotted fur of a leopard, historically traded as a luxury material
senses.definitionCN: 豹的皮或斑纹毛皮，历史上作为贵重材料流通
senses.example: The museum no longer displays its leopard skins.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆不再展出馆藏的豹皮。
senses.why: Anything valued in the market is traded by its material, so the animal name came to mean the commodity.
senses.whyCN: 凡在市场上受追捧的东西都会被当作材料买卖，动物名因此也指这种商品。

senses.title: A big cat of mountainous snow country
senses.definition: in compounds such as snow leopard, a pale long-tailed big cat of Central and South Asian mountains
senses.definitionCN: 在 snow leopard 等复合词中，指中亚与南亚高山地区毛色浅、尾巴长的大型猫科动物
senses.example: Snow leopards hide among cliffs where few people can climb.
senses.exampleCN: 雪豹藏在很少有人能爬上去的悬崖之间。
senses.why: Compound names extend leopard to related cats as a general label for spotted hunters.
senses.whyCN: 复合命名把 leopard 扩成「带斑纹的猎手」这一泛称，用来指相近的猫科动物。

intro.en: Leopard comes through Latin and Greek from a compound that sets the lion beside another big cat, likely of Asian or Persian origin.
intro.cn: leopard 经拉丁语和希腊语传来，源头是一个把「狮」与另一种大猫并列的复合词，后一种很可能是亚洲或波斯来源的外来词。

items.en: Greek leopardos joins leon, lion, with pardos, the name of another spotted big cat.
items.cn: 希腊语 leopardos 由 leon（狮子）与 pardos（另一种带斑纹的大型野猫的名字）组合。

items.en: Late Latin leopardus carries the name into European writing.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 leopardus 把这个名字带进欧洲文献。

items.en: Old French lepart and lebard show the word being reshaped in speech.
items.cn: 古法语 lepart、lebard 等写法显示它在口语中不断被改造。

items.en: Middle English leonpard borrows the word in this earlier, two-part shape.
items.cn: 中古英语以 leonpard 这种更古老的两段式形式借入。

items.en: The modern spelling settles by the sixteenth century, though some early printers inserted a letter or two by mistake.
items.cn: 到十六世纪拼写定型为现代形式；更早的印刷者曾误插进一两个字母，并非真实来源。

items.en: The word widens into leopard print, leopard skin, and compounds such as snow leopard.
items.cn: 现代英语中它扩展到豹纹、豹皮以及雪豹等复合词。

note.en: Leopard is one of the great cats, easily confused with cheetah and jaguar, and shaped by the Greek pardos element.
note.cn: leopard 属于大型猫科「猛兽家族」，容易与 cheetah、jaguar 混淆，构词上保留着希腊语 pardos 的痕迹。

entries.definition: an old term for a leopard or panther
entries.definitionCN: 古语中「豹、黑豹」的称呼，正是 leopard 后半段的来源

entries.definition: the large tawny social cat
entries.definitionCN: 狮子，对应 leopard 前半段的 leon；注意英语拼写不按词源还原

entries.definition: a female leopard
entries.definitionCN: 母豹，由 leopard 加阴性后缀构成

entries.definition: a slim spotted cat famous for speed
entries.definitionCN: 以冲刺速度闻名的细长斑点猫科动物，斑点小而圆，与 leopard 只拼写相近

entries.definition: a heavy spotted cat of the Americas
entries.definitionCN: 美洲的大型带斑猫科动物，体型更壮、斑纹中常带小点

entries.definition: a black-furred leopard or jaguar
entries.definitionCN: 黑豹，即毛色黑化的豹或美洲豹

normalIntro.en: Leopard carries two animals in one word: the lion half and the spotted pard half, which explains why it looks like lion in disguise.
normalIntro.cn: leopard 一个词里装了两只猛兽：狮子的那一半和带斑纹的 pard 那一半，所以它看起来像披着狮子皮的豹子。

normal.en: The first syllable echoes lion, because Greek leon meant lion.
normal.cn: 第一个音节让人联想到 lion，因为希腊语 leon 就是狮子。

normal.en: The second half comes from Greek pardos, an old word for a spotted cat.
normal.cn: 后半段来自希腊语 pardos，是古人对带斑纹大猫的称呼。

normal.en: Snow leopard keeps leopard as a general label for spotted hunters.
normal.cn: snow leopard 把 leopard 当作「带斑纹的猎手」的泛称来用。

normal.en: Leopard print is the coat pattern transferred to fabric.
normal.cn: leopard print 是把豹的毛皮花纹挪到了布料上。

normal.en: The female form is leopardess, the young is a cub.
normal.cn: 母豹是 leopardess，幼崽叫 cub。

abstract.en: Picture a pale yellow cat lying along a branch with its long tail hanging down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只淡黄色大猫趴在树枝上，长尾巴垂向地面。

abstract.en: See the rosette spots dissolve into the dappled shade of leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象梅花斑与叶片间的斑驳光影融成一片。

abstract.en: Think of a leopard print scarf glowing on a black coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一条豹纹围巾在黑色大衣上格外显眼。

examples.en: Leopards hunt at night and rest in trees during the day.
examples.cn: 花豹在夜间捕猎，白天在树上休息。

examples.en: The zoo bought a leopard print rug for the children area.
examples.cn: 动物园为儿童区买了一块豹纹地毯。

examples.en: Snow leopards live above the tree line in central Asia.
examples.cn: 雪豹生活在中亚的树线以上地区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累趴的」——豹子追了半天猎物累得趴下，正合它天性好隐藏、爱伏击的习性；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 leopardos = leon「狮子」+ pardos「带斑纹的大猫（很可能是亚洲、波斯来源的外来词）」；晚期拉丁语 leopardus → 古法语 lepart → 中古英语 leonpard → 现代英语 leopard。pardos 的确切来源存疑，一般认为源自伊朗语或中亚语言。

sensesIntro.en: Leopard begins as the animal itself, then lends its coat to the pattern, then to the skin as material, and finally names related cats in compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: leopard 起先是动物本身，随后毛皮花纹被借走成为印花，再作为材料指豹皮，最后在复合词里指相近的猫科动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale yellow cat with dark rosettes lies along a branch, half lost in leaf shadow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只淡黄色带深色梅花斑的大猫伏在树枝上，几乎融进叶影里。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: the living hunter is the primary sense and the source of all others.
branches.cn: 动物线：活着的猎手是首要义项，也是其余义项的来源。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: the spotted coat becomes a print used in clothing and design.
branches.cn: 花纹线：斑点毛皮变成服装与设计里的豹纹印花。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: the skin itself was valued and traded as a luxury item.
branches.cn: 材料线：豹皮本身被珍视，作为贵重商品流通。

branches.en: The cat and its mountain relatives are grouped under one name in compounds.
branches.cn: 豹与它的山地近亲被同一个名字收进复合词里。

branches.en: Pattern and material both reduce the living animal to a surface.
branches.cn: 花纹与材料都把活生生的动物缩减成了一个「表面」。

intro.en: Leopard is a compound loan drawn from Greek leon and pardos, with English compounds such as snow leopard built on top.
intro.cn: leopard 是由希腊语 leon 与 pardos 组成的借词复合体，英语又在上面叠出 snow leopard 这类新复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin leopardus and the adjective pangolin-like pardalis show how the Greek elements were refitted in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 leopardus 以及形容词 pardalis 的用法，显示出希腊语成分如何在拉丁语中被重新组装。

items.example: Leon is the first half of the ancient name.
items.exampleCN: leon 是古老名字的前一半。

items.example: Pardos gives the second half of the name.
items.exampleCN: pardos 提供名字的后一半。

items.example: Leopardus is the Latin bridge form.
items.exampleCN: leopardus 是拉丁语桥梁形式。

items.example: Leopard settles the modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: leopard 是现代拼写的定型形式。

items.example: The plural counts several animals.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式表示多只动物。

items.meaningCN: 表示雌性动物或女性的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ess forms leopardess.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ess 构成 leopardess。

items.example: Snow leopard is a modern compound on the old name.
items.exampleCN: snow leopard 是在旧词上生成的现代复合词。

items.example: Leopard print transfers the coat to cloth.
items.exampleCN: leopard print 把毛皮花纹移到布料上。

items.example: Leopardine adds the Latin adjective tail.
items.exampleCN: leopardine 加了拉丁语形容词词尾。

items.meaningCN: 黑豹（毛色黑化的豹或美洲豹）
items.example: Panther is a companion great-cat name from Greek.
items.exampleCN: panther 是另一个同样来自希腊语的猛兽名。

definition_zh: 减少；减轻；变小；贬低
definition_en: to become or make something smaller in size, amount, force, or degree
core_image: 一个沙漏里的沙子越漏越少，量在往下走
scene: 期末考试临近，紧张的气氛在教室里一点点淡下去。As the exam date approached, the tension in the room seemed to lessen.
sceneCN: 这里 lessen 是「减少、减弱」（第 2 个义项：程度或强度变小）；句意：考试日期临近时，房间里的紧张气氛似乎减弱了。

pos.zh: 贬低；轻视（少用，多为正式或古旧色彩）

derivatives.zh: lessen 加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「减少；减轻」
lessen 加过去分词后缀与否定前缀 un-，义为「未减少的」
lessen 的形容词与副词词干，义为「更少的；较少地」

senses.title: To become smaller in size or quantity
senses.definition: to become smaller in size, number, or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量上变得更少
senses.example: The noise from the street lessened after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜过后，街上的噪音变小了。
senses.why: The verb was formed directly from less, so its first job is simply to name the act of getting less.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接从 less 造出动词，所以最本义就是把「变少」这个动作说出来。

senses.title: To weaken in force or degree
senses.definition: to become or make weaker in force, intensity, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在力量、强度或程度上变得或使变得较弱
senses.example: Painkillers helped to lessen the pain within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 止痛药在一小时内帮助减轻了疼痛。
senses.why: Force and pain can also be measured as quantities, so less was easily extended from number to intensity.
senses.whyCN: 力量和疼痛也能按「量」来感觉，所以「更少」自然从数量扩展到强度。

senses.title: To reduce something deliberately
senses.definition: to make something smaller in amount or effect on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意使某物的数量或影响变小
senses.example: The company raised safety standards to lessen the risk of accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 公司提高了安全标准以降低事故风险。
senses.why: Once lessen is transitive it means a deliberate act, often with risk, cost, or damage as its object.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 lessen 用作及物动词，它常表示有意为之的动作，宾语多是风险、成本或损害。

senses.title: To look or seem less impressive
senses.definition: to become less impressive or important when compared with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与他人或他物相比时显得不那么出众或重要
senses.example: Her speech was strong until his reply lessened it in front of the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 她的发言本来很有力，直到他的回答在听众面前让它显得逊色。
senses.why: Something can also be lessened in reputation, which turns a drop in amount into a drop in standing.
senses.whyCN: 某物的声望也能被 lessen，这时数量的下降就变成了地位和分量的下降。

senses.title: To speak of someone with little respect
senses.definition: to describe someone or something as worth little
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物说成没什么价值
senses.example: Do not lessen your opponent just because she is young.
senses.exampleCN: 不要因为你的对手年轻就轻视她。
senses.why: Older usage keeps the idea of becoming less as a social judgment: a person is made less in the eyes of others.
senses.whyCN: 较早的用法把「变少」当作社会评价：某人在别人眼里被弄得小了、没有分量了。

senses.title: To fade in physical presence
senses.definition: to appear smaller or fainter as distance or time grows
senses.definitionCN: 随着距离或时间增加而显得更小、更淡
senses.example: The lights of the coast lessened as the ferry moved out to sea.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮驶向海上时，岸边的灯火渐渐暗淡下去。
senses.why: In a picture or a view, things really do get smaller as they recede, so the word also pictures fading away.
senses.whyCN: 在画面或视野里，远处的东西确实会变小，所以这个词也带着「渐渐消失」的画面。

senses.title: To make a burden lighter
senses.definition: to make a duty, feeling, or burden easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 使职责、情绪或负担更容易承受
senses.example: Neighbours came to lessen the burden on the family after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后，邻居们来减轻这家人的负担。
senses.why: A burden that is less is a burden that weighs less, which is why the word pairs naturally with load and duty.
senses.whyCN: 负担变少了，就是压在身上的重量变轻了，所以这个词常与负担、责任搭配。

intro.en: Lessen is the English verb of less, an adjective that Old English already had. It is not a borrowing from Latin, so the core idea is simply to get less.
intro.cn: lessen 是形容词 less 的英语动词形式，less 在古英语里已经存在。它不是拉丁语借词，核心意思就是「变得更少」。

items.en: Less is recorded as an adjective and adverb meaning not so great in amount.
items.cn: 古英语里 less 已经是形容词和副词，意为数量不那么大的。

items.en: The verb lessen is first recorded in the 1200s, formed by adding -en to the adjective.
items.cn: 动词 lessen 最早见于十三世纪，是在形容词后加 -en 构成的。

items.en: Lessen pairs with strengthen, lengthen, and fasten, all built with the same verb ending.
items.cn: 中古英语里 lessen 与 strengthen、lengthen、fasten 并列，都用了同一个动词词尾。

items.en: Lessen spreads from size and quantity to pain, noise, risk, and tension.
items.cn: 近代早期英语中 lessen 从大小、数量扩展到疼痛、噪音、风险和紧张。

items.en: The word is common in IELTS-style writing about reducing cost, risk, and impact.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个常见于写作场景，多与降低成本、风险和影响搭配。

note.en: Lessen sits between words of getting less, such as reduce and diminish, and spelling neighbours such as less and lesson.
note.cn: lessen 处在两组词之间：一边是表示「变少」的 reduce、diminish，一边是拼写相近的 less 与 lesson。

entries.definition: smaller in amount or degree
entries.definitionCN: 更少的；较少的

entries.definition: a period of teaching, or a warning example
entries.definitionCN: 课；教训（只是读音相同、拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a reduction
entries.definitionCN: 减少；减轻

entries.definition: to make something smaller on purpose
entries.definitionCN: 减少；降低（及物，强调有意为之）

entries.definition: to become gradually smaller or weaker
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐减少、削弱（较正式）

entries.definition: to make something less painful or difficult
entries.definitionCN: 缓解；减轻（疼痛或困难）

normalIntro.en: Remember that less plus the verb ending -en makes a verb meaning to get less, with no Latin root to argue about.
normalIntro.cn: 记住：less 加动词词尾 -en 就是「变少」的动词，没有拉丁词根需要绕。

normal.en: Less is the adjective, lessen is the verb.
normal.cn: less 是形容词，lessen 是动词。

normal.en: The ending -en is the same one found in strengthen and lengthen.
normal.cn: 词尾 -en 与 strengthen、lengthen 里的相同。

normal.en: Lesson has one s fewer in the middle, so it means a class.
normal.cn: lesson 中间少一个 s，意思是课。

normal.en: Lessen the risk is a very common IELTS phrase.
normal.cn: lessen the risk 是雅思写作中的常用搭配。

normal.en: Compare the pair: reduce acts on something, lessen can also act alone.
normal.cn: 对比一下：reduce 需要宾语，lessen 也可单独起效。

abstract.en: Picture sand running out of an hourglass until only a thin line is left.
abstract.cn: 想象沙漏里的沙子一直在少，最后只剩薄薄一层。

abstract.en: Think of the volume knob being turned slowly down.
abstract.cn: 想象把音量旋钮一点点拧小。

abstract.en: Imagine a heavy stone lifted step by step from shoulders that were bent.
abstract.cn: 想象把肩上的重石一级一级搬走。

examples.en: Regular exercise can lessen the risk of heart disease.
examples.cn: 经常锻炼可以降低心脏病的风险。

examples.en: The wind lessened towards evening and the boats went out.
examples.cn: 傍晚风力减弱，船只出海了。

examples.en: Careful planning will lessen the impact of the storm on the village.
examples.cn: 周密的规划会减轻风暴对村庄的影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累死能」——活越干越少，累感就减轻了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语形容词 less（较少）加动词词尾 -en 而成，核心义「使……变少」；同族有 lessening、unlessened。

sensesIntro.en: Lessen starts from getting less in size or quantity, grows into force and intention, and finally covers fading away and losing importance.
sensesIntro.cn: lessen 从数量、大小变少出发，延伸到力度与有意为之的行动，最后覆盖景象消退与分量降低。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sand running out until there is less than before.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙子不断漏出，剩下的比原来少。

branches.en: A drop in size or number comes first.
branches.cn: 大小或数量变少是最基础的义项。

branches.en: Fading in force and fading in view both mean getting smaller over time.
branches.cn: 力量和景象的消退，都是随时间变小。

branches.en: Deliberate reduction changes risk into a lighter burden.
branches.cn: 有意减少风险，就是把负担变轻。

branches.en: Social judgment makes a person or speech seem less in others eyes.
branches.cn: 社会评价让某人或某番话在别人眼里变小。

branches.en: Size, intensity, and action share one verb root.
branches.cn: 大小、强度与人为行动共享同一个词干。

intro.en: Lessen is a native English formation, not a Latin compound. Its parts are the adjective less and the verb ending -en.
intro.cn: lessen 是英语本土构词，不是拉丁语复合词。它的成分是形容词 less 与动词词尾 -en。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source word here, so the list of Latin cognates is empty; the family is English from less to lessening.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语源词，所以拉丁同族一栏为空；词族完全是英语，从 less 到 lessening。

items.example: Less is the adjective behind the verb.
items.exampleCN: less 是动词背后的形容词。

items.example: The ending -en changes an adjective into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 把形容词变成动词。

items.example: Lessen is the adjective turned into action.
items.exampleCN: lessen 就是形容词变成了动作。

items.example: The rain lessened by noon and we were lessened in our worry.
items.exampleCN: 中午雨小了，我们的担忧也减轻了。

items.example: A steady lessening of noise followed the traffic ban.
items.exampleCN: 限行之后噪音持续减少。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或动作的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成过程名词。

items.example: The prefix un- negates the participle.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 否定分词。

items.example: The cost remained unlessened after the talks.
items.exampleCN: 会谈之后成本仍未减少。

items.meaningCN: 加强（同构词，反义的动词）
items.example: Strengthen uses the same ending as lessen.
items.exampleCN: strengthen 用了与 lessen 相同的词尾。

items.example: Lengthen belongs to the same -en family.
items.exampleCN: lengthen 属于同一个 -en 构词家族。

definition_zh: 致命的；杀伤性的；危害极大的
definition_en: causing death, or extreme enough to be very dangerous or damaging
core_image: 一具身体被无形的死气抽干，像被死神带走一样
scene: 实验室的柜门上贴着醒目的警告标签，里面是极少量就能致死的药剂。A small bottle of lethal poison sat behind a warning label in the cabinet.
sceneCN: 这里 lethal 是「致命的」（第 1 个义项：能致死的）；句意：一小瓶致命毒药放在柜子里，柜门上贴着警告标签。

collocations.zh: 极其危险（甚至毁灭性）的组合

derivatives.zh: lethal 加 -ity，义为「致死性；杀伤力」
lethal 加 -ly，义为「致命地」
否定前缀 non- 加 lethal，义为「非致命的」

senses.title: Causing death
senses.definition: capable of causing death
senses.definitionCN: 足以致人死亡
senses.example: The bite of that snake can be lethal within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 那种蛇咬伤后几小时内就可能致死。
senses.why: The word grew out of the idea of death itself, so its first and clearest job is to label what causes death.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「死亡」这个概念本身长出来，所以最直接的就是标明能造成死亡的东西。

senses.title: Designed to kill
senses.titleCN: 为致死而设计的；杀伤性的
senses.definition: made or meant to cause death
senses.definitionCN: 被制成意图致死的
senses.example: Police officers admitted they were not trained to handle lethal force.
senses.exampleCN: 警员们承认他们没有接受过应对致命武力的培训。
senses.why: In weapons and warfare the purpose is built in, so lethal moves from a result to an intention.
senses.whyCN: 在武器与战争语境里，「致死」是被设计进去的目的，于是 lethal 从结果义变成了意图义。

senses.title: Extremely harmful in effect
senses.definition: extremely damaging or harmful, though not physically deadly
senses.definitionCN: 危害极大，但不一定真的致人死亡
senses.example: A few careless words can be lethal to the confidence of a young child.
senses.exampleCN: 几句漫不经心的话就可能严重打击幼童的自信。
senses.why: From poison and weapons the word stretches to anything that ruins a person or plan as surely as poison would.
senses.whyCN: 从毒药和武器出发，这个词扩展到任何能像毒药那样毁掉人或计划的事物。

senses.title: In a quantity that kills
senses.definition: used of a dose, concentration, or level high enough to kill
senses.definitionCN: 用于剂量、浓度或水平，指已达到足以致死的程度
senses.example: Tests showed a lethal dose of the chemical in the town water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 检测显示，镇上的自来水中有达到致死剂量的该化学品。
senses.why: Science turns the adjective into a measurable threshold, a set amount above which no body survives.
senses.whyCN: 科学用法把这个形容词变成可测量的阈值：超过某个量，身体就撑不住了。

senses.title: Bleakly funny
senses.definition: used of a joke or result that is bitterly funny, as if death itself were a punchline
senses.definitionCN: 指关于死亡的苦涩玩笑，结果或办法让人哭笑不得
senses.example: The two rival coaches traded lethal jokes about last season.
senses.exampleCN: 两位互为宿敌的教练拿上个赛季互相开着苦涩的玩笑。
senses.why: Humour plays with the same dark idea, using death imagery for mock attacks that do no real harm.
senses.whyCN: 幽默借用了同一个阴暗意象，用死亡的画面来开玩笑，实际并不真伤人。

intro.en: Lethal comes from Latin letalis, from letum death. Latin lex, law, has been suggested as a deeper link, but that origin is not certain.
intro.cn: lethal 来自拉丁语 letalis，源于 letum（死亡）。有说法认为更底层可追溯到拉丁语 lex（法律），但这一来源并不确定。

items.en: Letum is a poetic Latin word for death or ruin.
items.cn: letum 是拉丁语中表示「死亡、毁灭」的诗性词。

items.en: The adjective letalis means deadly or mortal.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语的形容词 letalis 意为致命的、必死的。

items.en: The spelling shifts to letalis with a single t in many texts, giving the English form.
items.cn: 后期的拉丁文本常把拼写写成单 t 的 letalis，这正是英语形式的来源。

items.en: Lethal enters English in the 1500s through scientific and medical writing.
items.cn: 十六世纪，lethal 经科学和医学文献进入英语。

items.en: Phrases such as lethal dose and lethal injection fix the word in modern law and science.
items.cn: 二十世纪，致死剂量、注射死刑等说法把这个词固定在现代法律与科学中。

note.en: Lethal belongs to a family of death words, and it also looks close to Lethe, a river of forgetting in Greek myth, and to the unrelated word lethargy.
note.cn: lethal 属于「死亡」词族，外形上又与希腊神话中「忘川」的名字接近。

entries.definition: the power to cause death
entries.definitionCN: 致死性；杀伤力

entries.definition: a river of forgetfulness in Greek myth
entries.definitionCN: 希腊神话中使人忘记前尘的忘川（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a state of unusual tiredness
entries.definitionCN: 无精打采；嗜睡（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: able to cause death
entries.definitionCN: 致命的（最普通的口语词）

entries.definition: causing death, often in an accident
entries.definitionCN: 致命的（多指事故或直接后果）

entries.definition: leading to death, or subject to death
entries.definitionCN: 致死的；必死的

normalIntro.en: Link lethal to the Latin word for death, letum, and keep in mind that it is a strong word, close to deadly but more formal.
normalIntro.cn: 把 lethal 与拉丁语中表示「死亡」的 letum 联系起来，同时记住它语气很重，接近 deadly 但更正式。

normal.en: Lethal dose is the amount that kills.
normal.cn: lethal dose 就是能致死的那一剂量。

normal.en: Lethal injection is the phrase behind execution by medical means.
normal.cn: lethal injection 指的是注射死刑。

normal.en: The noun lethality measures how deadly something is.
normal.cn: 名词 lethality 衡量某物有多致命。

normal.en: Fatal usually describes an accident, lethal often describes a substance or weapon.
normal.cn: fatal 多描述事故，lethal 多描述物质或武器。

normal.en: Non-lethal weapons are made to stop people without killing them.
normal.cn: non-lethal weapons 指不致死地制止对方的武器。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of water on a table with no life around it.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一杯水，四周没有任何活物。

abstract.en: Imagine a weapon marked with a skull.
abstract.cn: 想象一件标着骷髅的武器。

abstract.en: Think of a single harsh sentence crushing the confidence of a child.
abstract.cn: 想象一句苛责的话，把孩子整片自信压垮。

examples.en: The pesticide is lethal to birds and bees.
examples.cn: 这种杀虫剂对鸟类和蜜蜂是致命的。

examples.en: Mix those two cleaning agents and the result can be lethal.
examples.cn: 把这两种清洁剂混在一起，结果可能是致命的。

examples.en: A sudden lethal counter-attack unsettled the champions.
examples.cn: 这支球队杀伤力极强的反击让冠军队伍心神不定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离死」——离死不远处，就是致命的；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 letum（死亡）→ letalis（致命的）→ 英语 lethal，核心义「带来死亡的」。

sensesIntro.en: Lethal begins as a plain label for what causes death, then sharpens into purpose, threshold, and finally metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: lethal 最初只是标明「会造成死亡」，随后精确化为意图、阈值，最后走向比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unseen force that drains the life out of a body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股看不见的力量把身体里的生命抽干。

branches.en: Causing death is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 「能致死」是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Weapons and doses turn death into a design or a number.
branches.cn: 武器和剂量把死亡变成设计意图或一个数字。

branches.en: Metaphor lets ruin of confidence count as lethal.
branches.cn: 比喻让自信被毁也成了致命。

branches.en: Humour borrows death for jokes that do no harm.
branches.cn: 幽默借死亡的意象开玩笑，实际不伤人。

branches.en: The same death image serves plain warning and dark humour.
branches.cn: 同一个死亡意象，既用于严肃警告，也用于黑色玩笑。

intro.en: Lethal is a whole Latin adjective borrowed into English, with ordinary English endings added after it.
intro.cn: lethal 是整体借入英语的拉丁形容词，此后只在后面加普通英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin letum death and the adjective letalis give one short family, which English extends with -ity and -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 letum（死亡）与形容词 letalis 构成一个小词族，英语再用 -ity 和 -ly 扩展。

items.example: Letum is the Latin noun for death.
items.exampleCN: letum 是拉丁语中表示死亡的词。

items.example: The ending -alis turns a noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -alis 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Letalis passes into English as lethal.
items.exampleCN: letalis 进入英语后成为 lethal。

items.example: Lethal keeps the Latin meaning throughout.
items.exampleCN: lethal 一直保留拉丁语的词义。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms lethality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 lethality。

items.example: They measured the lethality of the gas.
items.exampleCN: 他们测量了这种气体的致死性。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms lethally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 lethally。

items.example: The dose was lethally high.
items.exampleCN: 这个剂量高到致命。

items.example: The prefix non- opposes the killing sense.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 non- 否定了致死之义。

items.example: Police used a non-lethal round.
items.exampleCN: 警方使用了非致命弹。

definition_zh: 生菜；莴苣；生菜叶；钱（俚语）
definition_en: a green leafy vegetable eaten raw in salads, or its separate leaves
core_image: 一大团绿色叶片挤在菜篮里，水珠顺着叶脉往下淌
scene: 沙拉碗里只铺着几片叶子，厨师把它们一片片摆开。The chef washed every lettuce leaf before adding it to the salad.
sceneCN: 这里 lettuce 是「生菜」（第 1 个义项：可生吃的叶类蔬菜）；句意：厨师把每一片生菜叶都洗干净，然后放进沙拉里。

pos.zh: 生菜；莴苣（可数、不可数均可）
生菜叶（用于三明治、汉堡）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，指不同品种或一棵棵的生菜
lettuce 加后缀 -less，义为「没有生菜的」
口语文体，形容「带生菜味的；像生菜的」

senses.title: The leafy plant eaten in salads
senses.definition: a garden plant grown for its large green leaves, eaten raw
senses.definitionCN: 为食用大而绿的叶片而种植的园艺作物，多生吃
senses.example: We grow tomatoes and lettuce in the back garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在后园种番茄和生菜。
senses.why: The Latin name lactuca was a leaved crop, so the word begins as the plant itself, not as a dish.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lactuca 本来就是一种叶用作物，所以这个词最先是植物名称，而不是菜式。

senses.title: Its leaves, or the material as food
senses.definition: the leaves of this plant, or the plant used as food without being counted
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物的叶子，或作为食材而不按棵数的用法
senses.example: Put a little lettuce in the sandwich under the bacon.
senses.exampleCN: 在培根下面夹一点生菜。
senses.why: Once the plant is cut, only leaves remain, so the food sense drops the counting and keeps the leaf.
senses.whyCN: 植株一旦被摘下就只剩叶子，所以食材义不再数棵，而是直接聚焦在「叶」上。

senses.title: A variety or breed
senses.definition: one of the cultivated types, such as iceberg or cos, counted as separate kinds
senses.definitionCN: 栽培出来的品种，例如卷心菜型、长叶型，按品种计数
senses.example: The farm now grows three crisp lettuces for the winter market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场现在种三种脆生菜供应冬季市场。
senses.why: Different leaf shapes earned their own names, and the plural lettuces came to mean kinds rather than single heads.
senses.whyCN: 叶形不同就各有名字，于是复数形式 lettuces 慢慢指「品种」而不只是「几棵」。

senses.title: The plant in the garden
senses.definition: the growing plant in a field, garden, or greenhouse, before harvest
senses.definitionCN: 未采收前在田地、菜园或温室中生长的植株
senses.example: Frost damaged the lettuce in the low corner of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻损伤了菜园低洼处种着的生菜。
senses.why: Gardeners talk about raising a head before it is ever eaten, which keeps the crop sense separate from the plate.
senses.whyCN: 种菜的人先谈「把它种大」，还没上桌就已经在用它，于是形成独立的作物义。

senses.title: Money, in slang
senses.definition: paper money, used in informal American speech
senses.definitionCN: 纸钞、钱，用于美国口语
senses.example: He pulled a thick roll of lettuce out of his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他从口袋里掏出一卷厚厚的钞票。
senses.why: American slang uses green notes like leaves: the green colour carries the word from salad to cash.
senses.whyCN: 美式俚语把绿色的钞票当成绿叶来看：颜色把这个词从沙拉带到了钱包。

senses.title: A useless or delicate person
senses.titleCN: 无用之人；娇气的人（口语）
senses.definition: someone easily damaged or of little use, used as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 容易受损或不顶用的人，用作贬称
senses.example: The coach called his weakest defender a lettuce.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把他最弱的后卫叫作废物。
senses.why: The leaf is soft and breaks easily, so the word once mocked people seen as soft or fragile.
senses.whyCN: 叶子又软又易折，所以这个词借来嘲笑那些被认为软弱、不经用的人。

intro.en: Lettuce goes back to Latin lactuca, which is linked to lac, milk, because the stems give a milky juice. French then cut the word down to laitue, and English took it in with forms such as lettue and lettice before settling on lettuce.
intro.cn: lettuce 可追溯至拉丁语 lactuca，源于 lac（奶），因为茎被折断时会流出乳白色的汁液。法语把词缩短为 laitue，英语先借作 lettue，后来定为 lettuce。

items.en: Lactuca names the lettuce plant, linked to lac milk for its milky sap.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lactuca 指生菜植株，因有乳白色汁液而与 lac（奶）相关。

items.en: Laita and laitue shorten the Latin word in French.
items.cn: 法语中的 laita、laitue 把拉丁词缩短。

items.en: Middle English borrows it as lettue, spelled with one or two t letters.
items.cn: 中古英语把它借作 lettue，拼写时常有一个或两个 t。

items.en: The variant lettuce appears and slowly wins out in standard spelling.
items.cn: 异体拼写 lettuce 出现，并逐渐在标准拼写中胜出。

items.en: Gardening names such as iceberg lettuce spread in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪，卷心生菜等园艺名称广泛流行。

items.en: The green colour of banknotes gives the slang sense of money.
items.cn: 钞票的绿色带来了俚语中「钱」的义项。

note.en: Lettuce has a small word family and a crowded salad field, so the groups below separate spelling relatives from other leafy foods.
note.cn: lettuce 词族不大，但所属的「叶菜」义场很拥挤，所以下面一组看形近，一组看同类食物。

entries.definition: a net of crossed strips
entries.definitionCN: 格子架；网格（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: an old spelling of lettuce, also a rare word for the plant
entries.definitionCN: 生菜在早期英语中的旧拼写之一，现代标准拼写已不用

entries.definition: the Latin name for lettuce
entries.definitionCN: 生菜的拉丁语名称，是英语词的直接来源

entries.definition: a round leafy vegetable with tightly packed leaves
entries.definitionCN: 卷心菜；洋白菜

entries.definition: a dark green leafy vegetable
entries.definitionCN: 菠菜

entries.definition: a curly green leaf cabbage
entries.definitionCN: 羽衣甘蓝

normalIntro.en: Lettuce shares its start with the Latin word for milk, because the plant bleeds a milky sap when cut.
normalIntro.cn: lettuce 的词根与拉丁语中的「奶」同源，因为这种植物被折断时会流出乳白色汁液。

normal.en: You buy a whole head of lettuce, not a single leaf.
normal.cn: a head of lettuce 就是一整棵圆圆的生菜。

normal.en: Iceberg lettuce is the crisp pale kind with little taste.
normal.cn: iceberg lettuce 指脆而味淡的卷心生菜。

normal.en: The plural lettuces is used for kinds or separate plants.
normal.cn: 复数 lettuces 用来指品种或一棵棵的植株。

normal.en: Lettuce often goes with salad dressing, but salad also means other dishes.
normal.cn: 生菜常和沙拉酱同用，但 salad 也可以指别的菜品。

normal.en: The root shared with lactose and lactic links lettuce to milk in form only.
normal.cn: 生菜与 lactose、lactic 共有的词根把二者在词形上连到奶，并非词义相连。

abstract.en: Picture a wet green leaf torn slowly along its stem, where a milky drop appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一片湿漉漉的绿叶从茎上慢慢撕开，渗出乳白色的汁液。

abstract.en: Think of a burger with a pale leaf sticking out of the bun.
abstract.cn: 想象汉堡包的面包里伸出一片浅绿色的生菜叶。

abstract.en: Imagine a wallet full of green notes that look like stacked leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱包里塞满绿色钞票，看着像堆叠的叶子。

examples.en: She tore the lettuce into small pieces and dressed it with lemon.
examples.cn: 她把生菜撕成小块，用柠檬汁调味。

examples.en: Iceberg lettuce keeps its crispness longer than most other kinds.
examples.cn: 卷心生菜比大多数品种更能长时间保持脆爽。

examples.en: Growers moved their lettuces inside the greenhouse to avoid the frost.
examples.cn: 种植者把生菜搬进温室，以免受霜冻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来蹄丝」——生菜叶子掐开，白丝像牛奶拉丝，来自蹄子底下；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lactuca（生菜，因有乳白汁液而与 lac「奶」相连）→ 古法语 laitue → 中古英语 lettue / lettuce，核心义「叶用的生菜」。

sensesIntro.en: Lettuce moves from the plant to its leaves, to kinds and crops, and finally to slang for money and for a frail person.
sensesIntro.cn: lettuce 从植株出发，到叶子、品种与作物，最后滑向俚语中的「钱」和「脆弱的人」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bundle of wet green leaves packed tightly together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束湿漉漉的绿叶紧紧挤在一起。

branches.en: The plant itself is the first sense.
branches.cn: 植株本身是第一个义项。

branches.en: The food sense keeps only the leaves.
branches.cn: 食材义只保留叶子。

branches.en: Kinds and growing plants come from garden talk.
branches.cn: 品种与作物义来自园圃里的说法。

branches.en: The green colour turns the leaf into money in slang.
branches.cn: 俚语借绿色把叶子变成了钱。

branches.en: Softness lets the leaf become a mild insult for a person.
branches.cn: 叶片柔软，于是也成了对人的轻微贬称。

intro.en: Lettuce is a borrowed word rather than a compound, so its parts are the Latin root lact- and the ordinary English ending -uce that French gave it.
intro.cn: lettuce 是整体借词，而不是复合词，所以它的成分是拉丁词根 lact- 与法语赋予它的英语词尾 -uce。

latinIntro.en: Latin lac, milk, gives the root lact-, seen in lactuca, lactation, and lactate, all linked to milk or milk-like sap.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lac（奶）给出词根 lact-，见于 lactuca、lactation、lactate，都与奶或乳状汁液相关。

items.example: The root lact- names milk and milk-like fluids.
items.exampleCN: 词根 lact- 指奶与类似乳汁的液体。

items.meaningCN: 拉丁语中构成植物名的词尾
items.example: Together they form lactuca.
items.exampleCN: 两者合成 lactuca。

items.example: Lactuca yields a milky sap when cut.
items.exampleCN: lactuca 被切时会流出乳白汁。

items.example: Lactation shares the root with lactuca.
items.exampleCN: lactation 与 lactuca 共享词根。

items.example: Lactate is used in sport science.
items.exampleCN: lactate 常用于运动科学之中。

items.example: French kept laitue from the Latin word.
items.exampleCN: 法语把拉丁词保留为 laitue。

items.example: Early English wrote lettue.
items.exampleCN: 早期英语写作 lettue。

items.example: Lettuce is the modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: lettuce 是现代拼写。

items.example: The ending -less forms a rare adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成少见的形容词。

items.example: A lettuceless salad is just leaves of something else.
items.exampleCN: 没有生菜的沙拉不过是别的叶子。

definition_zh: 白血病；血癌
definition_en: a serious cancer of the blood and bone marrow in which too many white blood cells are produced
core_image: 骨髓里堆满失控增生的白色血细胞，挤走了健康的红血球
scene: 医学生翻开教材，读到血癌这一章，注意到这个常被拼错的医学术语。In the textbook the medical student learned that leukaemia begins in the bone marrow.
sceneCN: 这里 leukaemia 是「白血病」（第 1 个义项：血液与骨髓的恶性疾病）；句意：医学生学习到白血病起源于骨髓。

derivatives.zh: 白血病（性）的，由疾病名加形容词后缀 -ic 构成
白血病发生机制，疾病名 + 希腊语 genesis（产生）
白血病前期的，pre-（在……之前）+ 疾病名 + -ic

senses.title: Cancer of the blood-forming tissues
senses.definition: a serious disease in which the bone marrow makes far too many abnormal white blood cells
senses.definitionCN: 骨髓产生过多异常白血球的严重疾病
senses.example: Leukaemia is a cancer of the blood and bone marrow.
senses.exampleCN: 白血病是一种血液和骨髓的癌症。
senses.why: Greek leukos white and haima blood give white blood, because pale abnormal white cells crowd out healthy ones.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 leukos 意为白色，haima 意为血液，合起来是「白色的血」，因为苍白的异常白血球排挤了健康血细胞。

senses.title: The acute form
senses.definition: a rapidly developing type of the disease that needs urgent treatment
senses.definitionCN: 发展迅速、需要紧急治疗的一类白血病
senses.example: Acute leukaemia can worsen within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 急性白血病可能在几周内恶化。
senses.why: Acute marks the fast-growing cells, so the general white blood disease narrows to its quickest form.
senses.whyCN: acute 标记的是快速增生的细胞，所以「白色血液」这个总称收窄到最急速的那一类。

senses.title: The chronic form
senses.definition: a slowly progressing type of the disease that may be monitored for years
senses.definitionCN: 进展缓慢、可能多年只需监测的一类白血病
senses.example: Chronic leukaemia is often found during a routine blood test.
senses.exampleCN: 慢性白血病常常在常规血检中被发现。
senses.why: Chronic marks the slower cells, showing that the same root image can stretch over a very long time.
senses.whyCN: chronic 标记的是较缓慢的细胞，说明同样的核心意象可以拉长到很长的时间跨度。

senses.title: The blood picture
senses.definition: the abnormal blood pattern of too many white cells and too few red cells or platelets
senses.definitionCN: 白血球过多、红血球或血小板过少的异常血液图像
senses.example: The blood film showed a typical leukaemia pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 血涂片显示出典型的白血病血象。
senses.why: Under a microscope the white crowd is visible, turning the disease into a countable blood picture.
senses.whyCN: 在显微镜下能直接看到白色细胞的拥挤，于是疾病被看成了一幅可以计数、可以描述的血象。

senses.title: The bone marrow site
senses.definition: the place in the bone marrow where the diseased cells are first produced
senses.definitionCN: 病变细胞最初产生的骨髓部位
senses.example: The disease starts deep in the bone marrow.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病变起源于骨髓深处。
senses.why: Because white cells are born in the marrow, the word points to a site as well as a condition.
senses.whyCN: 白血球诞生于骨髓，所以这个词除了指疾病状态，也指向一个发生地点。

senses.title: The patient and the family
senses.definition: the human situation of people living with the illness and those who care for them
senses.definitionCN: 与该病共同生活的人以及照料他们的人所处的处境
senses.example: Her family learned a great deal about leukaemia during the treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗期间，她的家人对白血病了解了很多。

definition_zh: 白血病；血癌（美式拼写）
definition_en: the American spelling of a serious cancer of the blood and bone marrow in which too many white blood cells are made

senses.title: Cancer of the blood-forming tissues
senses.definition: a serious illness in which abnormal white blood cells multiply in the bone marrow and crowd out healthy cells
senses.definitionCN: 异常白血球在骨髓中大量增生、排挤健康细胞的严重疾病
senses.example: Leukemia is diagnosed with blood tests and a marrow sample.
senses.exampleCN: 白血病通过血液检查和骨髓取样确诊。
senses.why: Greek leukos white and haima blood name the pale white cells that flood the blood.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 leukos 意为白色，haima 意为血液，命名的是灌满血液的苍白白血球。

senses.title: The American spelling itself
senses.definition: the simplified American form of the word for the blood disease, without the letter a
senses.definitionCN: 这种血液疾病名称去掉字母 a 后的简化美式写法
senses.example: American medical journals print leukemia without the second a.
senses.exampleCN: 美国医学期刊印这个词时省去第二个 a。
senses.why: The dropping of a follows a general American habit of simplifying the Latin digraph ae.
senses.whyCN: 省去 a 是美式拼写简化拉丁字母组合 ae 的一般习惯，使同一个词有了两种外形。

senses.title: The acute type
senses.definition: a fast-growing type of the disease that needs immediate treatment
senses.definitionCN: 生长迅速、需要立即治疗的一类疾病
senses.example: Acute leukemia can appear suddenly in young children.
senses.exampleCN: 急性白血病可能突然出现在幼童身上。
senses.why: Acute fixes the speed of the multiplying cells, so the general disease narrows to its quickest shape.
senses.whyCN: acute 固定了增生细胞的速度，于是总称收窄为最急速的形态。

senses.title: The chronic type
senses.definition: a slow type of the disease that may be watched over many years
senses.definitionCN: 发展缓慢、可能多年只需观察的一类疾病
senses.example: Chronic leukemia often needs monitoring rather than urgent care.
senses.exampleCN: 慢性白血病常常需要长期监测，而非紧急抢救。
senses.why: Chronic stretches the same marrow image across years, contrasting with the acute branch.
senses.whyCN: chronic 把同样的骨髓意象拉长到多年，与急性分支形成对照。

senses.title: Leukemia cells under a microscope
senses.titleCN: 显微镜下的白血病细胞
senses.definition: the abnormal immature white cells that fill the blood and marrow
senses.definitionCN: 充满血液与骨髓的异常未成熟白血球
senses.example: The lab counted leukemia cells in the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在样本中统计了白血病细胞。
senses.why: Once the disease is named, its abnormal cells become objects that can be seen and counted.
senses.whyCN: 一旦疾病被命名，它的异常细胞就变成了可以被看见、被计数的对象。

senses.title: Leukemia patients and families
senses.definition: the people living with the illness and the relatives who support them
senses.definitionCN: 与该病共同生活的患者以及支持他们的亲属
senses.example: Leukemia patients often spend long weeks in hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 白血病患者常常要在医院住上很长一段时间。
senses.why: A disease name also names the people inside it, so the word reaches the ward and the family.
senses.whyCN: 疾病名称也命名了身在其中的人，所以这个词延伸到了病房与家庭。

senses.title: Treatment and research
senses.definition: the chemotherapy, transplants and studies used to fight the disease
senses.definitionCN: 用于对抗该病的化疗、移植与研究工作
senses.example: New leukemia treatments target specific cell proteins.
senses.exampleCN: 新的白血病疗法针对特定的细胞蛋白。
senses.why: As a curable blood cancer, the word carries a branch of medicine and research.
senses.whyCN: 作为一种有望治愈的血液癌症，这个词自带一条通向医学与研究的分支。
