senses.title: A bar used to lift weight
senses.definition: a stiff bar that rests on a support so that a small force can lift a heavy object
senses.definitionCN: 压在支撑点上、能以小力抬起重物的硬棒
senses.example: A lever lets a light hand raise a heavy stone.
senses.exampleCN: 杠杆能让一只手轻轻抬起一块重石。
senses.why: From the Latin verb for raising, lever is literally the thing that raises.
senses.whyCN: 来源于拉丁语中「举起」的动词，lever 字面就是「用来举起的东西」。

senses.title: A handle that controls a machine
senses.definition: a part of a machine that a person pushes or pulls to make it work
senses.definitionCN: 机器上由人推拉来使其运转的部件
senses.example: He pulled the lever next to the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他拉下了门旁的操纵杆。
senses.why: A handle also lifts and releases something, so it inherits the nameless bar image.
senses.whyCN: 把手同样是在抬起或松开某物，于是也继承了那根硬棒的意象。

senses.title: The principle of reducing effort
senses.definition: the mechanical idea that effort and length of arm trade against each other
senses.definitionCN: 关于用力大小与力臂长短相互权衡的力学观念
senses.example: The lever principle explains why long handles feel light.
senses.exampleCN: 杠杆原理解释了为什么长把手用起来很轻。
senses.why: Once the bar works, people want the rule behind it, so the tool becomes a principle.
senses.whyCN: 硬棒一旦管用，人们就想知道背后的规则，于是工具变成了原理。

senses.title: A means of influence
senses.definition: something used to gain power or make others act as you wish
senses.definitionCN: 用来取得影响力或让别人照你的意愿行事的东西
senses.example: Trade is a strong lever in international talks.
senses.exampleCN: 在国际谈判中，贸易是有力的筹码。
senses.why: What moves a crate can also move a person, so leverage turns into the sense of influence.
senses.whyCN: 能撬动木箱的东西也能撬动人，于是杠杆意象转成了影响力。

senses.title: To move something with a bar
senses.definition: to raise or force something open using a strong bar
senses.definitionCN: 用结实的杆子把某物抬起或撑开
senses.example: They levered the lid off the box.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把箱盖撬了下来。
senses.why: Naming the tool later became the act of using it, a common verb-making path.
senses.whyCN: 先用名词称呼工具，后来动词化指「使用这个工具」，这是常见的造动词语径。

senses.title: Levers in the body
senses.definition: the bones and joints that work as levers during movement
senses.definitionCN: 运动中充当杠杆的骨骼与关节
senses.example: Our arm acts as a lever when we lift a weight.
senses.exampleCN: 举重时我们的手臂就像杠杆。
senses.why: The body offers a ready image of bars, supports and loads, so the word reaches anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 身体本身就提供了杆、支点与负载的画面，所以这个词也进入了人体解剖领域。

senses.title: Levers in finance
senses.definition: borrowed money used to increase the size of an investment
senses.definitionCN: 用来放大投资规模的借来的资金
senses.example: Too much lever can ruin a small company.
senses.exampleCN: 过高的杠杆率可能拖垮一家小公司。
senses.why: Money borrowed to amplify a return works like a bar: the same push moves much more.
senses.whyCN: 借钱放大收益就像一根硬棒：同样的力道能推动更多的东西。

intro.en: Lever comes from Old French lever, to raise, from Latin levare, to lighten or lift, which is related to levis, light.
intro.cn: lever 来自古法语 lever（举起），追溯到拉丁语 levare（使变轻、抬起），与 levis（轻的）同源。

items.en: Levis means light in weight.
items.cn: levis 意为轻的、不重的。

items.en: Levare means to make light or to lift.
items.cn: levare 意为使变轻或举起。

items.en: Lever means to raise or lift up.
items.cn: 古法语 lever 意为举起、抬起。

items.en: The word is recorded in English for a bar used to raise weights.
items.cn: 英语中记录该词，指用来举起重物的硬棒。

items.en: Physics texts fix the word in its mechanical sense.
items.cn: 物理学著作把该词固定为力学用语。

items.en: Lever also means a handle and, later, a means of influence.
items.cn: 现代英语中它还指操纵杆，后来又指影响手段。

note.en: Lever shares the Latin root levare with several English words of lifting, lightening and influence.
note.cn: lever 与若干表示「举起、减轻、影响」的英语词共享拉丁语词根 levare。

entries.definition: power to influence, or the action of a lever
entries.definitionCN: 影响力；杠杆作用

entries.definition: to demand and collect a tax
entries.definitionCN: 征收（税款）；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a young hare
entries.definitionCN: 小野兔；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a part you hold or turn
entries.definitionCN: 把手；握柄

entries.definition: an iron bar used for prising
entries.definitionCN: 撬棒；铁撬

entries.definition: a tool used for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 工具；手段

normalIntro.en: Lever comes from lifting: Latin levare, to raise, makes the bar that raises a weight.
normalIntro.cn: lever 源于「举起」：拉丁语 levare（抬起）造出了举起重物的硬棒。

normal.en: Leverage is the influence sense built on lever.
normal.cn: leverage 是在 lever 之上构成的影响力义项。

normal.en: A policy lever is a change that pushes an outcome.
normal.cn: policy lever 就是推动结果的一项改变。

normal.en: The levare root also gives relieve and elevate.
normal.cn: levare 词根还能构成 relieve 与 elevate。

normal.en: Compare handle: a handle is held, a lever is pushed against a load.
normal.cn: 对比 handle：把手用手握，杠杆则顶住负载发力。

normal.en: A lever needs a fulcrum, a load and an effort.
normal.cn: 杠杆需要支点、负载与作用力三者。

abstract.en: Picture a seesaw with a heavy box on one end.
abstract.cn: 想象一架跷跷板，一端放着一只重箱。

abstract.en: Imagine a finger pressing a long handle and a boulder moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一根长杆被手指轻压，巨石随之移动。

abstract.en: Think of money as a bar that multiplies a small push.
abstract.cn: 把资金想成一根能把小推力放大的硬棒。

examples.en: Insert the lever under the rock and push down.
examples.cn: 把杠杆插到石头下面，然后往下压。

examples.en: She pulled the lever to start the engine.
examples.cn: 她拉下操纵杆启动了引擎。

examples.en: Education is a lever for social change.
examples.cn: 教育是社会变革的杠杆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里沃」——把力留在里面、以巧劲拔升，就是杠杆在起作用；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 levis（轻的）→ levare（使变轻、举起）→ 古法语 lever（举起）→ 英语 lever（举物的硬棒），核心义「以举起为能事的硬棒」。

sensesIntro.en: Lever begins as a bar for lifting, grows into a machine handle and a principle, then into influence, a verb, and figures of the body and of finance.
sensesIntro.cn: lever 先是举物的硬棒，再长成机器的操纵杆与力学原理，随后演化为影响力、动词，以及人体与金融中的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stiff bar tilting on a fulcrum to raise a load.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根硬棒压在支点上，把负载撬起。

branches.en: The bar itself is the concrete everyday sense.
branches.cn: 硬棒本身是最具体的日常义项。

branches.en: The handle and the principle describe the bar at work.
branches.cn: 操纵杆与原理描述硬棒如何工作。

branches.en: Influence is the bar used on people.
branches.cn: 影响力就是把杠杆用在人身上。

branches.en: The verb records the act of prising.
branches.cn: 动词记录撬动这一动作。

branches.en: The body and finance repeat the bar image in new fields.
branches.cn: 人体与金融在新领域中重复了硬棒的意象。

intro.en: Lever is a whole Latin word carried into English, with a family built by -age and -ed.
intro.cn: lever 是一个整体借入英语的拉丁语词，并靠 -age 与 -ed 等词尾发展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin levare means to lift or lighten, and levis means light.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 levare 意为举起或减轻，levis 意为轻的。

items.example: A lever rests on a fulcrum.
items.exampleCN: 杠杆压在支点上。

items.example: Leverage amplifies a small effort.
items.exampleCN: 杠杆作用放大了很小的力。

items.example: The suffix -age forms leverage.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 构成 leverage。

items.example: A levered lid opens smoothly.
items.exampleCN: 带杠杆的盖子开启顺滑。

items.example: The prefix re- forms relieve.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 构成 relieve。

items.example: Relieve keeps the lightening sense.
items.exampleCN: relieve 保留了「使变轻」的含义。

items.example: Elevate uses the same lifting root.
items.exampleCN: elevate 使用同一条「抬起」词根。

items.example: Elevator means the thing that lifts.
items.exampleCN: elevator 意为「举起来的东西」。

items.example: Levitate names rising without support.
items.exampleCN: levitate 表示无支撑地升起。

items.example: Levy is only a spelling neighbour.
items.exampleCN: levy 只是拼写上的邻居，词源不同。

definition_zh: 词汇的；词语的；字面的；词法的
definition_en: relating to the words of a language, to the vocabulary rather than the grammar, or to the ordinary meaning of a word
core_image: 一本摊开的词典：每一个词条都像抽屉里贴好标签的小格子
scene: 老师把课上的生词单独列成一张表，说要先补词汇，再回头讲语法。The teacher drew up a separate list of new words and said the class would focus on lexical items before returning to grammar.
sceneCN: 这里 lexical 是「词汇方面的」（第 1 个义项：与词汇相关的）；句意：老师把课上的生词单独列成一张表，说要先补词汇，再回头讲语法。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语词根直接进入英语的名词，义为「词典；词汇总集」
语言学借用的希腊语名词，义为「一种语言的词汇系统」
lexic- 加学科后缀 -logy 构成，义为「词汇学」
lexic- 加希腊语 graphein（书写）构成，义为「词典编纂者」
加动词后缀 -ise 构成，义为「词汇化：把词组凝固成词」

senses.title: Relating to vocabulary
senses.definition: relating to the words of a language, especially to its vocabulary as distinct from its grammar
senses.definitionCN: 与一种语言的词语相关，尤其指与词汇相关，并与语法相对而言
senses.example: The study examines the lexical knowledge of young learners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究考察少年学习者的词汇知识。
senses.why: The base lexis names the stock of words in a language, so the adjective marks anything that belongs to that stock rather than to grammar.
senses.whyCN: 词根 lexis 指一门语言里词语的总和，因此这个形容词标记的是属于这份「词语库存」而非语法的东西。

senses.title: Of the literal meaning of a word
senses.definition: relating to the ordinary dictionary meaning of a word, as opposed to an extended or figurative use
senses.definitionCN: 指词语在词典里的通常意义，与引申或比喻用法相对
senses.example: The child understood the lexical meaning of the phrase but missed the joke.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子懂了这个短语的字面意思，却没听出笑点。
senses.why: A lexicon lists meanings word by word, so lexical meaning is the meaning you would find printed beside the headword, before any poetic extension.
senses.whyCN: 词典逐条列出释义，所以「词汇意义」就是词条旁边印着的那个意思，尚未经过引申和诗意发挥。

senses.title: Of word formation and word classes
senses.definition: of or relating to the forms words take and the classes they belong to, such as nouns and verbs
senses.definitionCN: 与词语的形式以及名词、动词等词类归属相关
senses.example: Adding un- is a lexical change that alters the base word.
senses.exampleCN: 加前缀 un- 是一种改变基础词的构词变化。
senses.why: When linguists speak of lexical categories, they treat a word as a stored dictionary unit, so its shape and part of speech become lexical properties.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家讲「词汇范畴」时，把词当作词典里储存的单位，于是它的形态和词性就成了这种单位自带的属性。

senses.title: In exam and teaching frameworks
senses.definition: in language testing, the range and accuracy of the vocabulary a learner uses in speaking or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在语言测试中指学习者在口语或写作中使用的词汇的广度与准确度
senses.example: A strong lexical resource lifted her writing score.
senses.exampleCN: 丰富的词汇资源提高了她的写作分数。
senses.why: Test rubrics borrow the word for the size and precision of a learner word store, turning an abstract category into a score.
senses.whyCN: 考试评分标准借用了这个词，用来描述学习者「词库」的大小与精准度，把抽象范畴变成了一项分数。

senses.title: Expressed by words rather than by grammar
senses.definition: of a meaning expressed by a particular word rather than by grammar or word order
senses.definitionCN: 指某种意义由具体词语承载，而不是由语法结构或语序表达
senses.example: Past time is lexical in the phrase last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 在 last winter 这个短语里，过去时间是由词语本身表达的。
senses.why: Languages can say that something happened yesterday either with a tense ending or with a word such as yesterday, and the second route is called lexical.
senses.whyCN: 语言既可以用时态词尾表示「昨天发生了」，也可以直接用 yesterday 这样的词，后一种方式就被叫作「词汇的」。

intro.en: Lexical comes from Greek lexis, speech or a way of speaking, from legein, to gather and then to speak, through the Latin adjective lexicus and its modern Latin base lexic-.
intro.cn: lexical 来自希腊语 lexis（说话、言辞），源于动词 legein（收集，引申为说、讲），经由拉丁语形容词 lexicus 以及现代拉丁语词干 lexic- 进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root leg- carries the sense of gathering or collecting, the earliest layer behind the word.
items.cn: 重构的原始印欧语词根 leg- 含有「收集、聚集」的意思，是这个词最早的一层来源。

items.en: Legein moves from gathering to picking out words and speaking, and the noun lexis means a word, speech, or a way of speaking.
items.cn: 希腊语 legein 从「收集」发展为「挑选词语、说话」，名词 lexis 意为词、言语或说话方式。

items.en: The neuter adjective lexikon, short for lexikon biblion, means a book of words, and gives English lexicon and the combining form lexic-.
items.cn: 中性形容词 lexikon 是短语「词语之书」的省略说法，进入英语的 lexicon 以及构词成分 lexic- 都出自这里。

items.en: Scholars writing in Latin coin lexicus for what belongs to words, and English draws on this Latin stem for its adjective.
items.cn: 用拉丁语写作的学者造出 lexicus 表示「属于词语的」，英语的形容词正是从这个拉丁词干借来的。

items.en: Lexical enters English in the first half of the nineteenth century in philological writing and grows into a common term of linguistics.
items.cn: lexical 在十九世纪上半叶随语文学写作进入英语，后来成为语言学的常用术语。

note.en: Lexical sits inside the lex- family of lexicon, lexis, and lexiology, and its near neighbours are words about vocabulary, word choice, and formal bookish language.
note.cn: lexical 属于 lexicon、lexis、lexicology 这一 lex- 词族，它的近邻是与词汇、用词以及书面雅语相关的词。

entries.definition: the vocabulary of a language, or a dictionary
entries.definitionCN: 一门语言的词汇总集，或词典

entries.definition: the total stock of words in a language
entries.definitionCN: 一种语言的全部词语

entries.definition: the study of the vocabulary of a language
entries.definitionCN: 对一种语言词汇的研究，即词汇学

entries.definition: relating to words, especially spoken ones
entries.definitionCN: 与词语相关的，尤指口头上的（并非同一词根）

entries.definition: the particular words used to say something
entries.definitionCN: 某段话所用的具体措辞

entries.definition: relating to meaning in language
entries.definitionCN: 指语言意义的，关注的是意义而非词语本身

normalIntro.en: Lexical keeps the Greek lex- stem of lexicon and lexis, so every memory hook that starts from a dictionary or a word list lands on the right meaning.
normalIntro.cn: lexical 保留了 lexicon、lexis 的希腊语词干 lex-，所以任何从词典或单词表出发的记忆钩子都会落到正确的意思上。

normal.en: The headword of a dictionary is a lexicon entry, and lexical means belonging to the world of such entries.
normal.cn: 词典的词条就是 lexicon 里的一条，lexical 指属于这种词条世界的。

normal.en: In language study, grammar covers how words fit together and lexical covers the words themselves.
normal.cn: 在语言学习里，语法管词怎么搭配，lexical 管词本身。

normal.en: Lexical meaning is what a dictionary prints beside the word, before any figurative twist.
normal.cn: lexical meaning 就是词典印在词旁边的那个意思，还没经过比喻的弯折。

normal.en: The noun lexis names the whole word store, and the adjective lexical points to anything in that store.
normal.cn: 名词 lexis 指整个词语仓库，形容词 lexical 则指向仓库里的任何东西。

normal.en: Compare lexical with semantic: lexical is about the word, semantic is about the sense it carries.
normal.cn: 对比 lexical 与 semantic：前者说的是词，后者说的是词承载的意义。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of labelled drawers, each drawer holding one word.
abstract.cn: 想象一排贴好标签的抽屉，每只抽屉里放着一个词。

abstract.en: Imagine flipping through a dictionary until one headword stops your finger.
abstract.cn: 想象翻词典，直到某个词条让你的手指停下来。

abstract.en: Think of a sentence as bricks of words set in the mortar of grammar.
abstract.cn: 把句子想成用语法当灰浆砌起来的词语砖块。

examples.en: Candidates who use a wide range of lexical items tend to score higher.
examples.cn: 使用丰富词项的考生往往得分更高。

examples.en: The translator preserved the lexical meaning but lost the rhythm.
examples.cn: 译者保留了字面意义，却丢掉了节奏。

examples.en: Recent studies show that lexical knowledge predicts reading speed.
examples.cn: 近期研究表明，词汇知识可以预测阅读速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来可搜」：碰到生词就打开词典「来可搜」一搜，搜到的都是词汇——lexical 就是「词汇的」。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始印欧语重构词根 leg-（收集）→ 希腊语 legein（收集、说话）与 lexis（言辞、词）→ 中性形容词 lexikon（词语之书，即词典）→ 现代拉丁语词干 lexic- + 形容词后缀 -al → 英语 lexical，核心义「与词有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Lexical starts from the whole vocabulary of a language, narrows to the literal sense stored in a dictionary, then to word forms and word classes, then to measured vocabulary in exams, and finally to meaning expressed by words rather than by grammar.
sensesIntro.cn: lexical 先指一门语言的整个词汇，再收窄到词典里储存的字面意义，然后指词的形态与词类，接着指考试中可衡量的词汇量，最后指由词语而非语法表达的意义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dictionary open at one headword, each entry a labelled drawer of words.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本翻到某词条的词典，每条词目都是贴着标签的词语抽屉。

branches.en: The basic sense covers everything that belongs to the vocabulary of a language.
branches.cn: 基本义项涵盖一门语言词汇范围内的一切。

branches.en: The dictionary sense names the plain meaning printed beside a word.
branches.cn: 词典义项指词条旁印着的平实意义。

branches.en: Word forms and word classes are properties of the stored word.
branches.cn: 词形与词类是作为储存单位的词语自带的属性。

branches.en: Exam rubrics turn the vocabulary into a score for range and accuracy.
branches.cn: 考试标准把词汇量转化为广度与准确度分数。

branches.en: Both senses answer the same question of which part of a language a given word belongs to.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在回答同一个问题：某个词属于语言的哪一部分。

intro.en: Lexical is built from the Greek word stem lex-, found in lexicon and lexis, plus the Latin adjective ending -al, and the same stem feeds lexis, lexicology, and lexicographer.
intro.cn: lexical 由希腊语词干 lex-（见于 lexicon、lexis）加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al 构成，同一词干还派生出 lexis、lexicology 与 lexicographer。

latinIntro.en: Greek legein means to gather and then to speak, lexis means speech, and the phrase lexikon biblion means a book of words; the Latin adjective lexicus and the stem lexic- carry the word into English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 legein 意为收集、进而说话，lexis 意为言语，短语 lexikon biblion 意为「词语之书」；拉丁语形容词 lexicus 与词干 lexic- 把它带进了英语。

items.example: The stem lex- appears in lexicon and lexis.
items.exampleCN: 词干 lex- 出现在 lexicon 与 lexis 中。

items.example: The suffix -al turns the stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 把词干变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ic is used in lexic before another suffix follows.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 用在 lexic 里，后面再接其他后缀。

items.meaning: the words of a language, a dictionary
items.example: Lexicon is the noun behind lexical.
items.exampleCN: lexicon 是 lexical 背后的名词。

items.example: Lexicography means the writing of dictionaries.
items.exampleCN: lexicography 意为词典编纂。

items.example: Lexicology names the study of vocabulary.
items.exampleCN: lexicology 指对词汇的研究。

items.example: Lexicalise means to turn a phrase into a word.
items.exampleCN: lexicalise 意为把短语变成词。

items.example: The adverb lexically marks the vocabulary point of view.
items.exampleCN: 副词 lexically 标记词汇视角。

items.example: A lexicographer collects words into a lexicon.
items.exampleCN: 词典编纂者把词语收进词典。

latinEntries.meaning: of words, a book of words

definition_zh: 词典编纂者；词典编纂学家
definition_en: a person who writes, compiles, or edits dictionaries and studies how words should be recorded
core_image: 一位伏案的老者，桌上摊着写满卡片的大木盒，一张卡片记一个词
scene: 实习编辑问主编，为什么词典里要保留那么多冷僻旧词；主编说自己只是个词典编纂者，不敢删掉读书人还要查的词。A young editor asked why the dictionary kept so many rare old words, and the editor in chief, a lifelong lexicographer, said she could not throw away words that readers might still look up.
sceneCN: 这里 lexicographer 是「词典编纂者」（第 1 个义项：编写词典的人）；句意：年轻的编辑问，为什么词典要保留这么多冷僻旧词；一生做词典编纂的主编回答说，她不能丢掉读者还可能去查的词。

derivatives.zh: 由词干 lexic- 加希腊语 -graphy（书写）构成，义为「词典编纂；词典学」
由 lexicography 加后缀 -ic 构成，义为「词典编纂的」
lexicographic 加 -al 构成的同义形容词，义为「词典编纂方面的」
词干 lexic- 加 -logy（学科）构成，义为「词汇学」，与词典编纂分工不同
同一词干的名词原形，义为「词典；词汇总集」

senses.title: A writer or editor of dictionaries
senses.definition: a person whose work is to collect, define, and arrange the words of a dictionary
senses.definitionCN: 以收集词语、撰写释义并编排词典为职业的人
senses.example: The headword list was checked twice by a lexicographer.
senses.exampleCN: 这份词目表由一位词典编纂者核对了两遍。
senses.why: Greek graphein means to write and lexikon names a book of words, so a lexicographer is literally a writer of wordbooks.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 graphein 是「写」，lexikon 是「词语之书」，所以 lexicographer 字面上就是「写词语之书的人」。

senses.title: A dictionary scholar
senses.titleCN: 词典学家；词典学研究者
senses.definition: a scholar who studies how dictionaries are made and how words are described and selected
senses.definitionCN: 研究词典如何编成、词语如何被描写与取舍的学者
senses.example: As a lexicographer, she wrote about how usage labels are chosen.
senses.exampleCN: 作为词典学家，她写过关于用法标签如何选取的文章。
senses.why: At universities the job becomes research: the same title now names the person who theorises about dictionaries rather than the one who simply writes them.
senses.whyCN: 在大学里，这份工作变成了研究：同一个称谓现在指为词典建立理论的人，而不只是动手编写的人。

senses.title: One who records changing usage
senses.definition: a person who tracks how words change in meaning and usage and decides what to record in a new edition
senses.definitionCN: 追踪词语意义与用法的变化，并决定新版词典收录什么的人
senses.example: Lexicographers added the new slang only after it had lasted a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这些俚语流行了十年之后，词典编纂者才把它收进词典。
senses.why: Because a dictionary follows rather than leads, the lexicographer watches common speech like a recorder, marking when a sense has settled enough to be written down.
senses.whyCN: 词典是跟着语言走的，所以编纂者像记录员一样盯住日常说话，判断某个新义是否已经稳定到可以写进书里。

senses.title: Collector of words as data
senses.titleCN: 语料收集者；词汇整理人
senses.definition: a person who gathers large samples of real language and analyses them in order to describe vocabulary
senses.definitionCN: 收集大量真实语言样本并加以分析，以便描写词汇的人
senses.example: The lexicographer searched a corpus of two billion words.
senses.exampleCN: 这位编纂者在二十亿词的语料库里检索。
senses.why: Modern work rests on evidence, so the historical role of collecting quotations turns into the database job of counting and comparing real usage.
senses.whyCN: 现代工作以证据为基础，于是历史上摘抄引文的角色，变成了在数据库里统计、比对真实用法的角色。

senses.title: In everyday praise or blame
senses.titleCN: （日常用法）给词语下判决的人
senses.definition: in popular speech, someone who decides and polices what words are acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 在日常说法里，指决定并管束哪些词可以用的人
senses.example: Good luck telling a lexicographer which words are banned.
senses.exampleCN: 想跟词典编纂者讲哪些词该禁，怕是很难说服对方。
senses.why: Readers imagine a lexicographer as a judge of correctness, though most of them insist they only record, and this split gives the word its ironic everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 读者把编纂者想象成「正确用法」的裁判，而大多数编纂者坚持自己只是记录者，这一分歧让这个词带上了调侃的日常用法。

intro.en: Lexicographer joins Latin lexicon, a book of words, to Greek graphein, to write, and the title was given to the sixteenth century Greek scholar Robert Estienne.
intro.cn: lexicographer 由拉丁语 lexicon（词语之书）加希腊语 graphein（书写）构成，这个称号最早用在十六世纪希腊语学者罗伯特·埃蒂安纳身上。

items.en: Legein gathers and speaks, lexis names speech or a word, and the neuter adjective lexikon means of words and stands short for lexikon biblion, a book of words.
items.cn: 希腊语 legein 兼有「收集」和「说出」之意，lexis 指言语或词，中性形容词 lexikon 意为「词语的」，是「词语之书」的省略说法。

items.en: Latin borrows lexikon as lexicon, the title early scholars gave to a Greek word list.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 lexikon 作 lexicon，早期学者用它称呼希腊语词表。

items.en: The element -graphos means writing or the act of writing, so the second half of the modern word comes from graphein, to write.
items.cn: 构词成分 -graphos 意为「书写」或「书写行为」，所以现代词的后半部来自 graphein（写）。

items.en: Lexicographer is given to Robert Estienne, a French printer and scholar of Greek, in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: lexicographer 在十七世纪被用来称法国印书家、希腊语学者罗伯特·埃蒂安纳。

items.en: The word spreads widely after Samuel Johnson published his dictionary of English in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 十八世纪塞缪尔·约翰逊出版英语词典之后，这个词广泛流行起来。

items.en: In the twentieth century the title also covers the new profession of corpus based and digital dictionary editors.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个称谓又覆盖了以语料库和数字技术为主的词典编辑这一新兴职业。

note.en: Lexicographer shares the combining form -grapher with geographer and biographer, and sits close to dictionary makers, dictionary science, and ordinary word-inventory words.
note.cn: lexicographer 与 geographer、biographer 共享构词成分 -grapher，并靠近「编词典的人」「词典学」以及普通的词汇名称。

entries.definition: the work or study of making dictionaries
entries.definitionCN: 词典编纂的工作或学问

entries.definition: the study of the vocabulary of a language
entries.definitionCN: 研究语言词汇的学问，与编词典分工不同

entries.definition: relating to dictionary making
entries.definitionCN: 与词典编纂相关的

entries.definition: a dictionary, especially of an ancient language
entries.definitionCN: 词典，尤指古代语言的词典（是编纂者编的东西）

entries.definition: a book that lists words with their meanings
entries.definitionCN: 列出词语及其释义的书，来自不同词根

entries.definition: a scholar who studies texts and historical language
entries.definitionCN: 研究文本与历史语言的学者，范围比编纂者更宽

normalIntro.en: Lexicographer reads as lexicon plus grapher, a wordbook plus a writer, so the long title simply says the person whose craft is writing dictionaries.
normalIntro.cn: lexicographer 可以拆成 lexicon 加 grapher，即「词语之书」加「书写者」，所以这个长词说的就是「以写词典为业的人」。

normal.en: The noun lexicography names the whole craft, and -er on the end marks the person who practises it.
normal.cn: 名词 lexicography 指这门手艺整体，词尾 -er 则标记从事这门手艺的人。

normal.en: Latin lexicon means a book of words, literally from Greek lexikon biblion.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lexicon 意为词语之书，字面来自希腊语短语「词语之书」。

normal.en: Samuel Johnson and Noah Webster are the two names most often attached to lexicographer in English writing.
normal.cn: 在英语写作里，塞缪尔·约翰逊与诺亚·韦伯斯特是最常与 lexicographer 联系起来的两个名字。

normal.en: Lexicographer differs from lexicologist: one writes the dictionary, the other studies vocabulary as a science.
normal.cn: lexicographer 与 lexicologist 不同：前者写词典，后者把词汇当作一门科学来研究。

normal.en: The stress falls on the syllable before graph, so the word is spelled and pronounced lex-i-Cog-ra-pher.
normal.cn: 重音落在 graph 之前那个音节上，所以要读成 lex-i-COG-ra-pher。

abstract.en: Picture a desk covered in small cards, each card holding one word and one sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一张铺满小卡片的书桌，每张卡片记一个词和一句例句。

abstract.en: Imagine a craftsman cutting a thin slot into a long shelf so that one small label can slide in.
abstract.cn: 想象工匠在长书架上切出一条细缝，好让一个小标签滑进去。

abstract.en: Think of a gardener labelling every plant in a large greenhouse, one label at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象园艺师在温室里一株一株地给植物贴标签。

examples.en: The lexicographer spent three years deciding which new senses to include.
examples.cn: 这位词典编纂者花了三年时间决定收录哪些新义项。

examples.en: She became a lexicographer after working on a historical dictionary.
examples.cn: 她在参与一部历史词典之后成了一名词典编纂者。

examples.en: Most lexicographers insist that they record usage rather than rule on it.
examples.cn: 大多数词典编纂者坚持，他们只记录用法，而不裁决用法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克西狗瑞佛」：一位老大爷牵着小狗，在镇上挨家「来克」收集词语，再一字一「佛」般把词供进词典——他就是词典编纂者。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 legein（收集、说话）与 lexis（言辞）→ lexikon（词语之书）→ 拉丁语 lexicon（词典）＋ 希腊语 graphein（书写）→ 英语 lexicographer，核心义「写词语之书的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Lexicographer begins as the craftsman who writes a wordbook, then widens to the scholar who studies dictionaries, then to the recorder of changing usage, then to the modern corpus researcher, and finally to the everyday figure whom some wrongly treat as a judge of correctness.
sensesIntro.cn: lexicographer 先指动手编写词语之书的匠人，再扩展到研究词典的学者，然后指记录用法变化的人，接着指现代靠语料库工作的研究者，最后指日常口语里被误当作「正确用法裁判」的那个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card box holding one word per card, written by one careful hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只卡片盒，一张卡片一个词，全由一只认真的手写成。

branches.en: The central sense is the person who assembles a dictionary.
branches.cn: 中心义项是汇编词典的那个人。

branches.en: The university sense makes dictionary making an object of study.
branches.cn: 大学义项把编词典本身变成研究对象。

branches.en: Watching language change is the recorder sense of the role.
branches.cn: 盯住语言变化，是这个角色的记录者义项。

branches.en: Corpus work turns collecting into counting, so the old card box becomes a database.
branches.cn: 语料库工作把「收集」变成了数据库时代的统计。

branches.en: Both senses come back to the question of whether the lexicographer records or rules.
branches.cn: 两个义项都绕回同一个问题：编纂者只是记录，还是在裁决。

intro.en: Lexicographer joins lexic-, from Greek lexikon, a book of words, to -grapher, from Greek graphein, to write, and the same pieces build lexicography, lexicographic, and lexicon.
intro.cn: lexicographer 由 lexic-（来自希腊语 lexikon，词语之书）加 -grapher（来自希腊语 graphein，书写）构成，同样的构件还组成 lexicography、lexicographic 与 lexicon。

latinIntro.en: Greek legein means to gather and to speak, lexis means speech, and lexikon biblion means a book of words; graphein means to write, and Latin lexicon carries the first half into English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 legein 意为收集、说话，lexis 意为言语，lexikon biblion 意为「词语之书」；graphein 意为书写，拉丁语 lexicon 把前半部分带进英语。

items.example: The stem lexic- points to the wordbook half of the job.
items.exampleCN: 词干 lexic- 指向这份工作里「词语之书」的那一半。

items.example: Lexicography is the writing of lexicons.
items.exampleCN: lexicography 就是词典的书写工作。

items.example: The ending -grapher names the person who writes.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -grapher 指动手书写的人。

items.example: Lexicon supplies the first half of the title.
items.exampleCN: lexicon 提供了这个称谓的前半部分。

items.meaning: a person who writes about the earth
items.example: Geographer shares the -grapher ending.
items.exampleCN: geographer 与它共享 -grapher 词尾。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms lexicographic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 lexicographic。

items.example: The suffix -al forms lexicographical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 lexicographical。

items.example: Lexicology is the sister field that studies vocabulary.
items.exampleCN: lexicology 是研究词汇的姊妹学科。

items.example: The ending -er marks the person, as in lexicographer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 标记那个人，lexicographer 就是如此。
